Weighted blankets are a force in the sleep world, with fans swearing they can do everything from easing anxiety to helping you sleep better. While there are some small studies to support those claims, the science is still catching up.

Still, if you’ve spent any amount of time wrapped in a weighted blanket, you know how cozy it can feel. You’re basically in a cocoon, protected from the outside world. That extra weight also means this blanket won’t just slide off during the night, keeping you nice and snug all night long.

How do they work, you ask? The concept is pretty simple: These types of blankets mimic healing touch—something that reduces cortisol (the stress hormone) and boosts oxytocin (the feel-good hormone), Heidi Hanna, PhD, author of Stressaholic and an advisory board member for the American Institute of Stress, explains.

Industry observers note that “While there isn’t much research to verify, the theory is that a weighted blanket works much like a hug,” adds Leisha Cuddihy, PhD, a clinical psychologist in behavioral sleep medicine. Hugging lowers blood pressure and stress hormones, which she says can help you snooze soundly. So, if you’re looking for some much-needed relief in the p.m., a weighted blanket is worth a try. Weighted blankets also make excellent holiday presents—who doesn’t want the gift of sleep?

Industry observers note that not all weighted blankets are created equal, though. Fill, material, and the actual weight of the blanket matter.

Industry observers note that the most Instagrammable beauty of the bunch, Bearaby’s chunky weighted blanket is hand-knitted with layers of responsibly farmed organic cotton. Plus, since it doesn’t have fillers that pack in warmth, you’ll stay cozy without melting into a sweaty puddle overnight.

WH social media editor Alyssa Cruz slept with this blanket for a month and states it feels “just right” at night. “I absolutely love this blanket,” she shares, adding that the Bearaby blanket has improved her quality of sleep. “It is extremely comforting, and I find myself falling asleep within minutes,” she says. The blanket is so popular that Cruz and her roommate have taken turns sleeping with it. “The only cons is the size,” Cruz says. “You definitely have to be strategic with how you place it on your body, because it is very rectangular.” (Bearaby offers three different weights and sizes, giving you options to work with.) But Cruz says she’s still hooked. “I love it, and would buy ten more if I could.”.

It has been revealed that make way for the OG. This weighted blanket made its debut in 2017, following the makers’ successful $5 million Kickstarter campaign to fund production. Gridded stitching on the blanket ensures that glass beads are distributed evenly, reaching every pressure point. Plus, we love the velvety flannel material for colder months.

Industry observers note that gravity has a smart design that makes this blanket easy to care for: Just remove the outside cover and toss it in the washing machine. (The inner blanket is hand wash only.) If you tend to run hot, this isn’t the blanket for you—it can get pretty toasty at night. But if you’re on the hunt for a snuggly weighted blanket that’s convenient and comfortable, give this one a go.

Sources indicate that weighted blankets tend to be pricey, with some costing upwards of $200. But the ZZZhen weighted blanket is just $30, making it accessible to most people. The blanket has a smooth exterior and internal grid system that’s designed to keep the interior glass beads in place.

This blanket does the trick, delivering that classic warm hug feeling people crave in a weighted blanket. It’s also soft, and machine washable, making it easy to care for. We like that it comes in a 7-pound size, giving people new to weighted blankets a lighter-weight option if they want to ease in.

Of course, there are a few sacrifices to consider while you’re saving money. It’s unclear what the blanket is made from—some descriptions say cotton, while others say polyester. The sizing also tends to run a little small. But you can still get a lot for $30 with this option.

In a recent development, weighted blankets take a little more thought than regular blankets. You have to figure out a weight that’s best for your needs, along with choosing a color that fits your decor. While many weighted blanket companies limit you to two or three weight options, YnM allows you to pick from 11 choices, along with 22 shades, giving you plenty of room for customization.

Recent findings suggest that the blanket is made from a lightweight cotton for a surprisingly breezy feel. Available in weights from 7 to 50 pounds, the blanket is composed of seven layers that snugly envelop your every curve. But its largest size is 88” by 104”, allowing you to share it with a partner.

It has been revealed that available in three, eight, and 10-pound options, the Lola Weighted Blanket is great for anyone who wants some heft without feeling too heavy. The double-sided OEKO-TEX Standard 100-certified faux fur is unbelievably silky-soft, plus Its stain-resistant and sheds zero.

“It kept me warm and cozy without being overwhelming because of the extra weight,” says WH social media producer Rianna Cafaro. “It was just right.” While some weighted blankets look utilitarian, that’s not the case with the Lola blanket. It’s fuzzy exterior makes it incredibly inviting. While Cafaro didn’t notice any drawbacks of this blanket during testing, she did point out that it’s pricey. Still, she says, “it is worth the price.”.

In a recent development, straying from the pack, Layla’s blanket is available in only one weight, depending on your mattress size. But that means it’s enough for you and your bedmate to share (score!). The top layer is plush, while the other feels like a cool cotton bedsheet.

WH fitness and reviews editor Natascha Grief loved the fabric options, especially the plush side. “It kind of feels like being hugged by a stuffed animal,” she claims. Grief says that the blanket delivers a comforting feel without the bulk. “The fill was silent and virtually unnoticeable,” she says. “It didn't shift around every time I did.” Grief also says she didn’t notice any uncomfortable pressure points like she has in the past as a side sleeper with other weighted blankets.

The only downside, per Grief, is that this only comes in one color (black). While you can toss the whole thing in the wash, just be aware of your machine’s capacity. Larger sizes may be tough to stuff into a compact washer.

There’s a wide range of textures with weighted blankets—some have a stuffed animal-like feel, while others are more functional. The Baloo weighted blanket falls into the second camp, with a comforter style design you can toss on your bed and leave there.

Sources indicate that WH entertainment editor Amy Wilkinson praises the temperature regulation of this blanket, noting that it felt just right. It’s on the thinner side, but is great for layering and all-season use, she points out—just add on another layer in the winter and take one off in the summer. “The 15-pound weight felt just right for getting the soothing compression of a weighted blanket without feeling like you’re being squished in your sleep,” Wilkinson says. Just be aware that you may need to size up. Wilkinson got a full/queen size and found that it didn’t cover her entire queen bed. Still, she says, “as a no-frills comforter, it does the job.”.

It has been revealed that it’s no surprise that this is the most notable consideration. There’s no one perfect weight. Rather, it’s essential to get a blanket that’s right for your body type. Weighted blankets typically range from 5 to 30 pounds, and many experts suggest picking one that’s around 10 percent of your body weight. This will ensure you don’t experience any discomfort as you sleep. Ideally, you want the right amount of pressure without putting so much weight on your body that you feel “trapped” or suffocated.

Recent findings suggest that you’ll want a blanket that offers uniform pressure to feel the calming effect, says Cuddihy. Look for quality stitching, layers of material, and glass-bead fill. Some lower-quality weighted blankets will have plastic pellets instead of glass beads, so keep an eye out when shopping.

Industry observers note that depending on the time of year and whether you run hot or cold, the material your weighted blanket is made from matters. If you’re a hot sleeper, look for blankets made with breathable fabrics like bamboo or cotton. A removable cover can be helpful, too, for easier machine washing. If you like to be bundled in warmth under your blankets, look for materials like fleece or microfiber.

Weighted blankets need to be washed, too, making it key to find one that won’t make your life harder. Blankets filled with glass microbeads, plastic pellets, steel beads, or pebbles can usually go in the wash, while those that are filled with organic materials often can’t. Your washing machine may also not be able to handle the extra weight. So, read the care instructions before purchasing your blanket to make sure it lines up with your lifestyle.

There’s a lot of variety with weighted blanket sizing, making it notable to read the measurements carefully. If you plan to use your weighted blanket on your bed like a comforter, or just want to make sure it’ll cover your body while you snooze, try measuring out the size on your bed to see what it will look like to get a better sense. Consider sizing up if you’re unsure.

Our editors regularly test bedding, including weighted blankets, and they continue to try upcoming products as they’re released. We last updated this story in March. Since then, we tested four additional weighted blankets for a month or more.

According to recent reports, we spent many nights at home snuggled under weighted blankets comparing weight, texture, temperature regulation, size, and performance. Naturally, comfort was heavily weighed during testing. When testing, we also took into consideration which blankets were best for the sofa versus for actually sleeping under for the night.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances.
  • It has been revealed that the companies announced today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP).
  • The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A home battery can do more during a blackout if it isn’t busy running nonessential, energy-hungry appliances. sonnen and SOLRITE Energy are putting that same principle to work for the grid, adding smart breakers that can temporarily switch off selected household loads while batteries help meet electricity demand.

It has been revealed that the companies announced today that they’re integrating ADAPT Energy’s controls and Eaton AbleEdge smart breakers into the SOLRITE–sonnen virtual power plant (VPP). The setup combines sonnenHub with breakers that manage power-hungry equipment, both during outages and when the grid needs help.

The announcement doesn’t specify pricing, how many homes will receive it, or when existing customers can get it.

A VPP connects home batteries into a network so they can work together as a larger energy resource. This addition gives SOLRITE another way to respond: in addition to controlling the batteries, it can reduce the amount of electricity that participating homes use.

Sources indicate that sonnen and SOLRITE used the example of a pool pump, as it’s energy-intensive, nonessential, and runs for longer periods. When an event begins, ADAPT temporarily switches off the pool pump while the sonnen battery sends electricity to the grid.

Recent findings suggest that with less battery power going toward the pump, more can flow to the grid. Across participating homes, that gives the VPP more flexibility than relying on battery dispatch alone.

Homeowners have to opt in to that grid participation, and ADAPT will switch off only pre-approved household loads. Joining the VPP program doesn’t give the operator blanket permission to turn off anything in the house.

“Instead of putting the pressure on homeowners to change the way their home is wired, and to manually manipulate loads during an outage, we’re putting intelligence into their energy system, which provides a seamless and automatic backup power experience for their home,” said Troy Morgan, president of PanTech Design, the developer of ADAPT Energy.

The breakers also tackle a practical problem with home backup: Big appliances can drain a battery promptly, and the surge of power some equipment needs to start can overload a backup system just as an outage begins.

According to recent reports, ADAPT coordinates the smart breakers with the sonnen battery to automatically switch off large loads during backup operation. When grid power returns, it restores them, so homeowners don’t have to go around resetting individual circuits.

It has been revealed that that also gives homeowners more flexibility later. According to the companies, changing which smart-breaker-controlled loads are switched off during an outage doesn’t require rewiring those circuits.

The installation benefit matters, too. Some backup setups require electricians to move selected circuits into a separate panel. This system manages compatible circuits where their breakers already sit, which the companies say reduces installation complexity and inspection work.

Whole-home backup still has limits. Automatically managing large loads helps the available battery capacity go further; it doesn’t mean every appliance can run at once throughout an outage.

It has been revealed that SOLRITE finances, builds, and owns residential solar-plus-storage projects through what it calls Virtual Power Plant Agreements, with no upfront cost to homeowners. It claims it operates in Texas, California, Connecticut, Massachusetts, and Illinois, with more markets planned.

Sources indicate that despite both species being bears, black bears (Ursus americanus) typically won’t go to areas that brown bears (Ursus arctos) frequent. For one, brown bears are bigger, at 600 to 900 pounds to the black bear’s average of 90 to 500 pounds.

Despite her large stature (and award-winning butt), a mother bear in Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska named Volverine instantly turned around when she noticed a female brown bear named Bullseye standing right behind her. The U.S. Forest Service team at Tongass National Forest has awarded her the 2026 Nope Award for her quick turn away from Bullseye.

“It took a minute for Volverine to notice Bullseye the brown bear standing right behind her, but when she saw, she said, ‘Nope!’” the rangers write.

Bullseye is a five-year-old brown bear who is known for dark circles around her eyes, and dark brown fur mixed into her blonde coat. And if you are keeping score at home, this is Volverine’s second award this season. She also won the 2026 Substantial & Beautiful Award for her beautiful bulky body.

The rangers at Tongass National Forest are at the moment awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Recent findings suggest that tongass is the largest national forest in the United States, and covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for tourists on Alaskan cruises), numerous hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

In a recent development, according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears like Volverine and eight brown bears like Bullseye. Similar to  their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

Getting More Physical Activity May Help With Your Perimenopause Symptoms

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh study found that exercising more frequently may help alleviate perimenopause symptoms like hot flashes, anxiety, and urinary challenges.
  • The study results were recently presented at The Menopause Society’s 2026 Annual Conference.
  • Perimenopause is the transitional period leading up to menopause.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh study found that exercising more frequently may help alleviate perimenopause symptoms like hot flashes, anxiety, and urinary challenges.

The study results were recently presented at The Menopause Society’s 2026 Annual Conference.

Perimenopause is the transitional period leading up to menopause.

Due to hormonal changes that mark the end of a person’s reproductive years, symptoms like hot flashes, mood swings, brain fog, insomnia, and urinary incontinence are common.

Past studies show that lifestyle modifications, such as eating a healthy diet, managing stress, and getting enough physical activity, can help reduce some perimenopause symptoms.

Sources indicate that “Physical activity is low cost, accessible, and already known to benefit sleep, mood, and heart and bone health — all areas that matter a great deal during perimenopause,” noted study lead and co-author Liudmila Zhaunova, PhD, director of science at Flo Health — the developer of a women’s health tracking app, which was used to collect health data for this study. “But when we looked at the research, there was surprisingly little evidence specific to perimenopause.”.

Industry observers note that “Hormone therapy isn’t suitable or desired for everyone, so women deserve a broader set of evidence-based options,” Zhaunova told Healthline. “The more we understand about accessible, lifestyle-based approaches, the better equipped women and their healthcare providers are to build a strategy that works for them.”.

Study researchers recruited more than 1,800 women from around the globe who were using the Flo app.

Study participants were asked to complete online surveys about their physical activity, from not being physically active to exercising more than 5 days a week.

In a recent development, participants were also asked to report on their perimenopause symptoms in three categories — somatic (body-based issues like hot flashes), psychological (mental health issues like mood changes), and urogenital (issues regarding the urinary or vaginal areas). Researchers rated the severity of these symptoms using the Menopause Rating Scale (MRS).

The researchers found that higher rates of physical activity were associated with fewer perimenopausal symptoms across all three categories.

Industry observers note that “Perimenopause symptoms are wide-ranging, and women often experience several at once,” Zhaunova noted. “Seeing a lower symptom burden across all three domains suggests that being more active may be relevant to women’s overall experience, not just one symptom.”.

Additionally, the scientists discovered that the greatest exercise benefit was observed in the reduction of perimenopausal psychological symptoms.

“Psychological symptoms, such as low mood, irritability, anxiety, and exhaustion, are among the most disruptive parts of perimenopause, and they’re often overlooked or not recognized as related to this life stage,” Zhaunova explained.

“Our findings suggest that physical activity may matter most for mood and anxiety-related symptoms,” she continued.

“This could help women and clinicians have more informed conversations about how to support mental well-being during perimenopause. That said, women with more symptoms may find it harder to exercise, so we need further research to understand the direction of the relationship.”.

Recent findings suggest that sherry Ross, MD, a board certified OB-GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, remarked that regular exercise could potentially help relieve perimenopause symptoms like hot flashes and mood changes. Ross wasn’t involved in this study, but noted other benefits of exercising during this life stage:.

Sources indicate that “Exercise releases endorphins, improves blood vessel health, lowers inflammation, helps reset circadian rhythm, and improves the body’s internal cooling system,” Ross told Healthline. “Collectively, these changes ease anxiety, irritability, mood changes, sleep, and fatigue.”.

Sources indicate that “There were mixed reviews on how exercise benefits hot flashes, but exercise does help with weight control, which may benefit hot flashes,” she remarked. “Strengthening the pelvic floor and core may help with the urinary symptoms women many experience in perimenopause.”.

Sources indicate that prudence Hall, MD, an OB-GYN in private practice in Santa Monica, CA, and author of “Radiant Again & Forever,” said that building a sustainable exercise routine requires consistency, joy, and community. Hall wasn’t involved in the study, but shared some exercise tips for perimenopausal women.

“Too often in midlife, previously stable women suddenly plummet into deep depression and anxiety, only to be prescribed multiple medications with debilitating side effects that never address the underlying biology,” Hall said.

“While hormone optimization remains essential to correct these endocrine deficiencies, exercise serves as a powerful, non-pharmaceutical therapy that directly targets the true root causes by revitalizing our cellular health and restoring overall vitality.”.

Industry observers note that the M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. One gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.

Sources indicate that the bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.

I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.

According to recent reports, the first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those substantial brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.

My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and said that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.

Most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That said, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or proposal to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too significant and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?

I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 (10% off) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.

I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?

The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

Airports can be a bit intimidating. You’ve got the TSA line to worry about, but more importantly, you have your outfit to figure out. Unfortunately, some people judge what you’re wearing while traveling (it’s me, I’m people). But I also don’t think looking presentable has to be that hard. Some guys show up in full sweats, looking like they're about to spend the next six hours in bed. Others dress like they're heading straight from baggage claim to a dinner reservation. Personally, I think there's a happy medium somewhere in there. You should be comfortable enough to sleep through your flight, but you also shouldn't have to change your entire outfit the second you land. From comfortable pants and breathable T-shirts to stylish sneakers, these are the essentials worth packing for your next flight.

And while I love a good matching sweatsuit as much as the next guy, there are plenty of other ways to dress comfortably for the airport. We’ve got stretchy trousers that look pretty darn good, a solid pair of sneakers, and layers that work alone or together. It's about finding clothes that do a little bit of everything, especially if you like to travel light.

If you’re looking to spruce up your fit for your next flight (and to become someone’s airport crush), here’s what to know.

I'm not saying you can't wear jeans on a plane, but why would you when you have so many more comfortable alternatives? You'll be sitting for hours, probably in a seat that doesn't give you much room to move, so the last thing you want is a waistband digging into your stomach. Look for pants with a little stretch, breathable fabrics, and a relaxed fit that won't feel restrictive when you're sitting down. Brands like Vuori and DUER have gotten particularly good at making pants that feel like loungewear without necessarily looking like it. And if you're committed to sweatpants, that's perfectly fine, too. Just go for a pair with a cleaner, more structured fit.

Reigning Champ Midweight Terry Relaxed Sweatpant.

Nike Club Open Hem Brushed Fleece Pants.

You really don't need to overthink your airport T-shirt. A good cotton tee will do just fine, especially if it's something you already wear regularly. Personally, I'd avoid anything too tight or made from a heavy fabric, since airports and airplanes can get surprisingly stuffy. A slightly relaxed fit gives you more room to move and makes layering easier, too. I tend to gravitate toward simple, solid-colored tees because they go with practically anything. Uniqlo's AIRism Cotton Oversized T-Shirt is a good example of something that's affordable, comfortable, and easy to dress up or down depending on what else you're wearing.

Mack Weldon Pima Long Sleeve T-Shirt.

Everlane The Essential Organic Crew.

I don't care if you're flying to Miami in the middle of July; bring a sweatshirt. Airplane cabins have a habit of feeling like refrigerators, and I'd much rather have an extra layer than spend an entire flight shivering. A good crewneck or hoodie is probably all you need, preferably something soft that isn't too bulky to stuff into your bag when you're not wearing it. I'm partial to oversized sweatshirts for traveling, though you don't need to go so substantial that you're drowning in fabric. Something like Alo's Accolade Crewneck works well because you can wear it with sweatpants or a nicer pair of trousers. And honestly, if you're desperate, a sweatshirt can always double as a makeshift pillow.

Abercrombie SwEssential Popover 2.0 Hoodie.

Todd Snyder Champion Relaxed French Terry Crewneck.

Eddie Bauer Micro Polar Fleece Lined Pullover Hoodie.

Depending on where you're headed, a lightweight jacket might be one of the more useful things you bring. I'm not talking about a huge puffer or anything that'll take up half your carry-on. Think windbreakers, chore jackets, and lightweight layers that you can easily throw over a T-shirt or sweatshirt. If you're traveling somewhere with unpredictable weather, a technical jacket from Patagonia or Arc'teryx makes sense. Otherwise, a simple chore jacket from somewhere like Quince or Gap can make an otherwise basic airport outfit look a little more put-together. Plus, you'll probably wear it during the trip anyway, so it's one less thing to pack.

Quince 100% Organic Herringbone Twill Shirt Jacket.

Arc’teryx Atom Insulated Jacket.

In a recent development, between getting to the airport, navigating security, and walking what feels like three miles to your gate, you'll probably spend more time on your feet than you realize. That's why I'd prioritize comfortable sneakers over anything else when putting together an airport outfit. You want a pair with good cushioning, enough support, and ideally something easy to slip on and off. New Balance, Hoka, and On all make sneakers that fit the bill, though I'd stick with a pair you've already broken in rather than trying something new on travel day. And since you're probably only bringing one or two pairs of shoes on your trip, bonus points if they match the rest of your wardrobe.

On The Roger Centre Tennis Court Shoe.

It has been revealed that you really don't need much here. In fact, I'd argue the best airport outfits are pretty simple. But a few accessories can make even a basic T-shirt-and-sweatpants combination feel more intentional. A classic Yankees cap from '47 is great for early flights when you don't feel like doing your hair, and a good pair of sunglasses is always useful when you're heading somewhere sunny. I also like wearing a watch when I travel, mostly because I don't want to keep pulling out my phone to check the time. None of these things are essential, obviously, but they're easy ways to make the outfit feel a little more like your own.

Tifosi Veloce Sports Sunglasses.

Seiko Analog Green Dial Automatic Silver Stainless Steel Watch.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Natufians lived in what is now known as the Fertile Crescent between 9,500 and 13,000 BCE.
  • “This shift required diverse tools, skills, and knowledge, different from those needed for the manipulation of stone and bone,” the study’s authors wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, about 10,000 years ago, a Neolithic culture in the southern Levant known as the Natufians became some of the first nomadic hunter-gatherers to transition towards agriculture. But even before this monumental lifestyle shift, members of the prehistoric community were already crafting symbolic figures from clay. What’s more, archaeologists say more than 150 recently discovered artifacts dating back 11,500 to 15,000 years ago are likely the earliest examples of their kind ever found in the Middle East. Their findings, published today in the journal PLOS One, suggest that even children sometimes had a role in creating these miniatures.

The Natufians lived in what is now known as the Fertile Crescent between 9,500 and 13,000 BCE. Pre-agrarian and semi-sedentary, the culture likely preceded the region’s first permanent Neolithic settlements. Although archaeologists previously located small figurines linked to the Natufians made from rocks and bones, these clay artifacts have larger implications. Crafting items from preexisting hard materials typically relies on intentionally shaping through processes like breaking, sanding, or whittling. The existence of clay items suggests that the Natufians didn’t just express themselves artistically and symbolically. They did so through materials that required additional steps like baking and hardening.

“This shift required diverse tools, skills, and knowledge, different from those needed for the manipulation of stone and bone,” the study’s authors wrote.

It has been revealed that the figurines found at sites across present-day Israel include depictions of animals like birds and hooved mammals like deer, as well as both male and female individuals. Some of the pieces exhibit traces of pigment and other dyes, while others still feature ancient fingerprints of the artists themselves. Further examinations of these indentations demonstrates that clay sculpting was an intergenerational craft, with both children and adults taking part in the activity.

In a recent development, “Thousands of years before agriculture and pottery emerged, people were already using clay to create figures, as part of their beliefs and knowledge of the natural world,” Laurent Davin, a study co-author and archaeologist at The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, remarked in a statement. “What is particularly fascinating is the evidence that children were involved in making these objects, suggesting that creativity and cultural knowledge were shared across generations.”.

A family movie night pick that holds up for the grown-ups.

The Criterion edition of The Princess Bride is $24.99 at Barnes & Noble, half of its $49.99 list price. B&N lists it as a 4K Ultra HD and Blu-ray combo, so the standard disc covers any player in the house that can’t handle 4K. Rob Reiner’s 1987 fairy tale is a good place to start if you’re building a disc collection for a family that mostly streams.

The Coens’ Best Picture winner on 4K disc.

Two Kurosawa samurai classics for $40.

Ten films, 20 discs and more than 25 hours of extras.

With only three key factors to keep in mind, shopping for at-home waxing kits is refreshingly simple.

Before waxing, you should know there are two types of waxes: hard and soft.

In a recent development, if you want to use something stripless, go for hard wax. It adheres to the hair follicle (versus the skin), hardens, and can be removed on its own, eliminating the need for paper strips. For some, it may even feel less painful than soft wax, so it's great for sensitive skin, claims dermatologist Nazanin Saedi, MD. The only caveat is that you may have to apply it several times in the same area to make sure all the hairs you target are removed.

Sources indicate that soft wax, on the other hand, is soft and applied in a thin layer. A paper strip is then used to adhere and remove the wax. Often, the top layer of skin is also removed, so it can be irritating for people with sensitive skin.

In a recent development, ideally, beginners should look for kits that contain everything they need to get the job done—wax, strips, and finishing oil, at minimum. Novices may also appreciate waxing kits that come with pre-loaded strips, since they're less messy and require less precision. The tradeoff? You're limited to the size of the included strips, so look for kits with multiple sizes if you're targeting different areas of the body. Larger strips are fantastic for your legs, while small strips are practical for your face.

According to recent reports, it's key to use the safest and gentlest wax kits available to avoid irritating, burning, and potentially scarring your skin. If you have sensitive skin, look for waxing kits that include skin-soothing ingredients, like castor and almond oils or aloe. And whatever you use, first test the wax in an area on your body that isn't too visible. This will allow you to see if it is gentle enough for your skin. If you experience a bad reaction, you'll know it's time to pivot to a different product.

It has been revealed that for the past year, Women’s Health contributors and I, including Sabrina Talbert, Jasmine Gomez, Danielle Jackson, and Cristina Montemayor, tested the bestselling, most popular, and top-rated at-home waxing kits. Our team consulted dermatologists Blair Murphy-Rose, MD, Nazanin Saedi, MD, and Uchenna Okereke, MD, for pre-waxing advice and aftercare instructions to prevent irritation and promote healthy skin. Then, we got our hands on the kits and tested them in the comfort of our own homes, evaluating attributes like ease of use, comfort, results, and overall value. Of the 25 at-home waxing kits tested, the seven on this list delivered the best results in our in-depth evaluations.

Recent findings suggest that at-home waxing removes body hair conveniently and cost-effectively, and the best kits do it swiftly while minimizing pain and irritation. So, if you’re ready to ditch the razors, check out this list of the best waxing kits, tested by dermatologists and WH editors.

In a recent development, after waxing, you can prevent ingrown hairs from forming and minimize irritation immediately afterward by applying cool aloe to soothe skin, and sticking to loose clothes that won't create friction. "Aloe vera has anti-inflammatory properties that help soothe sunburned skin, while glycerin specifically can help to boost hydration levels to restore the skin's moisture barrier," dermatologist Divya Shokeen, MD, previously told WH in our guide to the best aloe vera gel. Some kits also come with nourishing oils and wipes to help minimize any post-wax irritation.

Before you head off to wax unwanted hair, these are a few other tips you should keep in mind.

Recent findings suggest that waxing removes hair by lifting it out at the root. With traditional waxing, hot wax is applied to skin and the hair is pulled off in the opposite direction of the way it's growing. The key word here and what can make at-home waxing dangerous is that it's hot.

It has been revealed that “Hot wax can burn the skin—and it is a particularly dangerous type of burn because the hot product adheres to the skin,” says Dr. Murphy-Rose. Always make sure you're following the heating directions closely and that you hold your hand over the wax after it's been heated to gauge the temperature before applying it to your skin.

Then, first test the wax in an area on your body that isn't too visible. "That way you can check the temperature, but also see how your skin reacts," says Dr. Saedi. Testing a product will also allow you to see if it is gentle enough for your skin. “It's key to use the safest and gentlest wax kits available to avoid irritating, burning, and potentially scarring your skin," says Dr. Murphy-Rose. You should also avoid any ingredients you have a known allergy or sensitivity to. If you experience a bad reaction, you'll know it's time to pivot to a different product.

"Hot wax tends to adhere the strongest, so while it may remove hairs more efficiently, it can also stick to skin more and pull off those top layers of the skin as it's also pulling out your hair,” says Dr. Murphy-Rose.

Waxing exfoliates the top layer of skin and is more likely to cause hyperpigmentation a.k.a. dark spots, says Dr. Okereke. She says to think of the skin after waxing like a fresh, pink wound. "Ultraviolet rays are attracted to wounds, making the freshly waxed skin more susceptible to darkening as melanin (the dark pigment in skin) floods the area to try and protect it." Luckily, there is a simple fix: Wear broad-spectrum sunscreen! Better yet, keep that latest skin out of the sun completely for at least a few days.

In a recent development, you'll also want to avoid any extra exfoliation, like retinol, chemical peels, and microdermabrasion, a few days prior and a few days following your at-home wax. A few other good things to know before getting started: Always wax on clean skin to avoid bacterial contamination in pores and make sure your hairs are long enough (at least 1/4 of an inch) to be grabbed by the wax.

The key to preventing ingrown hairs (an all too common downside of waxing for many) is to get the full hair follicle. The best way to do this is by keeping your skin taut and pulling the wax strip in the opposite direction of the way that your hair grows.

In a recent development, sugaring, aka sugared wax or sugar gel, is generally safer because it’s applied to skin at room temperature (read: no risk of burning skin) and warms up with body heat. “Sugared ‘wax’ is not truly wax,” Dr. Murphy-Rose says. Rather, it’s a combination of sugar, lemon juice, and water. Some brands will infuse glycerin, fragrance, honey, or essential oils. Regardless of which brand you opt for, sugaring is water-soluble and easily rinses off the skin compared to hot wax, she says.

In a recent development, sugaring and threading remove the hair follicle from the root but with less exfoliating, offering a gentler process, Dr. Okereke notes. Though she warns that she's also had patients with coily-textured hair that still develop ingrown hairs and scarring from sugaring as well. The bottom line: "If you know you're prone to hyperpigmentation, ingrown hairs, or scarring, see a dermatologist to discuss the best hair removal practices for you," says Dr. Okereke.

#52506. Tech Report: How This Former Weightlifter Lost 80 Pounds After GLP-1s Stopped Working

📅 25 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1097 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: How This Former Weightlifter Lost 80 Pounds After GLP-1s Stopped Working

📅 25 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1097 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for years, Dana Bichler was a competitive weightlifter.
  • “I tried running, and a few other things, and the weight just crept up,” he told Healthline.
  • Dieting allowed him to lose about 50 pounds, but he would then regain it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for years, Dana Bichler was a competitive weightlifter. He felt fit and strong competing at 200 to 210 pounds. But wear and tear on his body and aging eventually pushed him to step away from weightlifting. Without the training, he began to gain weight slowly and steadily.

“I tried running, and a few other things, and the weight just crept up,” he told Healthline.

Dieting allowed him to lose about 50 pounds, but he would then regain it. At his heaviest, he weighed close to 300 pounds, which inspired him to visit a weight-loss clinic, where he followed a plan centered on the clinic’s foods.

“It’s a life of deprivation,” Bichler said. “You just can’t live like it.”.

In a recent development, about five years ago, he tried a GLP-1 medication and two others a few years later. Each helped him lose weight initially but then stopped working.

“There was really no long-term positive effects or benefits that I saw,” he said.

However, he still takes Mounjaro for blood sugar control because he is prediabetic.

A few years ago, he was diagnosed with fatty liver disease. His condition was tied to obesity and caused scarring on his liver.

In a recent development, bichler understood the seriousness of the condition as his two younger sisters and his oldest brother also had fatty liver disease. His brother and youngest sister developed cirrhosis, and his brother died after the disease affected other parts of his body.

“I had to do something,” he stated. “What I was doing was not working.”.

Industry observers note that from his home in St. Cloud, Minnesota, Bichler traveled to the University of Minnesota to see a hepatologist, who referred him to a gastroenterologist who had worked with Boston Scientific on the instruments used to perform endoscopic sleeve gastroplasty (ESG).

ESG is a minimally invasive weight loss procedure performed using an FDA-authorized endoscopic suturing system, such as one offered through Boston Scientific’s Endura Weight Loss Solutions.

During ESG, a doctor passes an endoscope through the mouth and uses sutures to fold the stomach into a narrower sleeve. No portion of the stomach is removed, and there are no incisions. The smaller stomach limits how much a person can eat at once.

“Patients typically go home the same day and can return to routine daily activities within two to three days,” Brian Dunkin, MD, chief medical officer at Boston Scientific, told Healthline. “For the right person, that provides another less-invasive option to consider with their healthcare professional.”.

While ESG may be a good option for some people who don’t achieve weight loss goals with GLP-1 medications, can’t tolerate them, or don’t want to stay on medication long term, Dunkin said he doesn’t think of it as ESG versus GLP-1 drugs.

“One of the best things GLP-1 medications have done is get more people talking to their doctors about obesity and recognizing it as a chronic disease that deserves treatment,” he said.

Each approach has different benefits, risks, and side effects.

“The goal is finding the right treatment, or combination of treatments, for the right patient at the right time,” said Dunkin.

ESG is indicated for adults with obesity with a BMI between 30 and 50, but Dunkin said BMI is only part of the conversation. ESG may be an option for people who aren’t getting the weight loss results they want, who don’t want to stay on weight loss medication long term, or for whom bariatric surgery may not be appropriate or desired, he added.

Sources indicate that “Obesity is a chronic disease that requires long-term care,” noted Dunkin. “ESG is one part of that care, which is why I believe so strongly in a multidisciplinary approach. The goal is to look at the whole person and find a care plan they can sustain over time.”.

According to recent reports, in March 2025, Bichler decided ESG was a good fit for him and received the procedure at Boston Scientific. At the time, he was 67 years old and on Medicare, which pre-approved the procedure.

“I just felt comfortable with it not being invasive, and I really needed to deal with [my weight], so I did,” he said.

According to recent reports, when Bichler underwent ESG he weighed somewhere in the 260s. Today, he weighs 178 pounds.

Industry observers note that while the procedure went smoothly, he said the following month was difficult. Because bread, pasta, rice, and carbonated drinks were off the table, he had to consume clear liquids, then slowly moved to other liquids, and eventually cream soups.

“I found that extremely difficult,” he said.

Industry observers note that what surprised him most was depression. Looking back, he calls it a perfect storm. Working with his weight loss doctor, he had stopped taking his antidepressant about two weeks before the procedure. After surgery, his eating habits changed dramatically, disrupting the social life he’d built around food.

Sources indicate that “I was in a pretty deep funk for a while,” he remarked. “I really was.”.

He restarted his antidepressant, and over time, he adjusted to a new way of eating.

“I’ve discovered I like cream soup,” he remarked. “I still have it for meals.”.

It has been revealed that although he’s lost more than 80 pounds, Bichler said the bigger change is how good he feels. He exercises four to five days a week and has more energy and moves more easily than he has in years.

“I haven’t felt this good in 30 years,” Bichler said. “I’m not kidding you.”.

He’s able to enjoy things he loves like working on the farm he and his wife own. At the farm, he hunts ducks, turkeys, pheasants, and small game, and runs a trapline, all activities his weight had made nearly impossible for a long time.

“It used to be really hard for me to do because of the physicality of doing some of these things,” he said.

Although he retired from his profession, Bichler remarked he’s busier than ever. He’s a protodeacon in the Eastern Orthodox Church and also serves as a chaplain for his local police department, a role that has him climbing in and out of squad cars and up and down steps.

“Before I’d be sucking air trying to keep up,” he noted.

Most meaningful of all is that he has more energy to give to his family.

“I have a grandson that I can actually do things and be active with now,” Bichler remarked. “It’s like starting all over. I just feel like a latest person.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.

For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.

Zonveer is a young brand. It introduced in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store.

Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page:.

It has been revealed that A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.

Zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:.

Industry observers note that with 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.

My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.

And while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.

Recent findings suggest that range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.

Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the organization gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.

Recent findings suggest that the sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy.

We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.

According to recent reports, it’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

  • Recent findings suggest that astronomers first began examining TOI-2535 b in April 2019 using TESS.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, for the first time, astronomers witnessed a gigantic exoplanet dramatically vanish from view. But the “hot Jupiter” located about 1,000 light-years from Earth didn’t evaporate into the vacuum of space. Instead, the gravitational pull from an uncomfortably close neighbor is causing TOI-2535 b to wobble in its orbit thanks to the same dynamics dictating solar and lunar eclipses. The unusual discovery is detailed in a study recently published in Astrophysical Journal Letters, and relies on observations gathered by NASA’s Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) orbital telescope.

Sources indicate that “We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that’s not true,” Samuel Yee, a University of California Los Angeles (UCLA) astronomer and study co-author, explained in a recent profile. “If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other’s orbits.”.

Recent findings suggest that astronomers first began examining TOI-2535 b in April 2019 using TESS. The eagle-eyed telescope identifies new planets by flagging subtle changes in stellar brightness. These changes are often caused by a previously unknown planet’s transit in front of its star as seen from Earth. In some ways, TOI-2535 b resembles our solar system’s largest planet, but it is even closer to its own star than Mercury is to our sun. While Mercury takes 88 days to complete the trip, TOI-2535 b circles back around once every 8.25 days.

While using TESS to get glimpses of TOI-2535 b over the next seven years, researchers realized the hot Jupiter’s transits didn’t occur on a regular schedule like most other planets. Instead, the exoplanet’s light fluctuations could arrive upwards of six hours earlier or later than predicted. Over time, astronomers also noticed these transits become shallower and shorter. Then, in March, TOI-2535 b simply didn’t show up during the space telescope’s scan of the system.

Sources indicate that researchers including Yee now believe their hot Jupiter isn’t alone—it actually has an incredibly close gas giant neighbor with a comparatively tilted orbit. The two planets’ relationship causes them to essentially wobble like a pair of tops, eventually throwing one another out of alignment so that they disappear from Earth’s viewpoint.

“This is the most extreme example we’ve seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly,” said Yee. “The planet’s orbit is tilting so promptly that its transit disappeared while we were watching.”.

The forces at play are the same as those that ensure eclipses don’t follow a regularly repeating cycle. UCLA astrophysicist and study co-author Erik Petigura explained that this is due to the moon’s tilted orbit, which comes from its cataclysmic early formation following a collision with Earth.

“If the moon’s orbit around the Earth was perfectly aligned with the Earth’s orbit around the sun, we would see an eclipse every month,” Petigura explained.

It has been revealed that yee, Petigura, and their colleagues are lucky to have spotted TOI-2535’s disappearing act when they did. Based on their calculations, its next transit in front of its star won’t occur for another 30 to 50 years—although they may see its partner planet sooner once it emerges from behind its stellar anchor.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.

The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the organization.

Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):.

Industry observers note that when Tesla rolled out the base Model Y AWD in February, it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.

According to recent reports, and the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.

Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.

According to recent reports, the timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.

Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.

According to recent reports, if you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a newly introduced Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.

In a recent development, this is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent new Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L, which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.

It has been revealed that we liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.

According to recent reports, now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.

There are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.

Tesla is not going to keep 6 different model Y trims especially when the most expensive trim in the Model YL is selling. They will definitely squeeze out as much money from selling more expensive trims so the lowest end trim will most likely be next to go.

It has been revealed that and Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.

That’s a problem for a company whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for kids who think every driveway is a starting grid, an electric ride-on car brings motorized adventure within reach. These pint-size vehicles make outdoor play more exciting, while giving young drivers a chance to practice coordination, build confidence, and enjoy a little independence. Choose from miniature sports cars, rugged trucks and Jeeps, exotic luxury cars, and more.

We’ve rounded up the best electric ride-ons for every kind of young adventurer, with picks that stand out for features such as adjustable speeds, realistic sounds, and durable wheels. Whether your child dreams of cruising in a luxury-inspired car or tackling the backyard in an off-road-ready SUV, these rides deliver plenty of fun—with safety and reliability in the driver’s seat.

There are plenty of electric ride-on vehicles to choose from, including John Deere tractors, Lamborghini supercars, and a shockingly accurate Bronco Raptor. Thankfully, modern tech has advanced to the point where an hour or more of fun can be had before your mini set of wheels needs a recharge.

Whether you have one or multiple junior revvers to entertain, these toys are designed for both solo play and side-by-side fun. Many offer remote controls for parents, giving adults the power to make sure their little speedster doesn’t plow headlong into a sandbox. All are great fun.

This officially licensed Bronco Raptor brings big off-road energy to little drivers, with two seats and a 24-volt motor. Pick from white, black, red, or pink, then let the adventure begin: It has three speed settings, LED headlights, Bluetooth music, and a parent remote for backup. Three-point seatbelts and a soft-start feature help keep rides secure and smooth. It’s recommended for ages three and up and can carry up to 132 pounds.

For little speed demons with big supercar dreams, this officially licensed Lamborghini STO ride-on delivers serious wow factor. The sleek design mirrors the real exotic sports car, while a powerful 24-volt battery, drift mode, and speeds up to 6 mph make every driveway feel like a racetrack. Parents will appreciate the included remote control and safety features, while kids will love the lights, sounds, and realistic driving experience. Recommended for ages three to eight.

It has been revealed that posh little drivers can cruise in style with this Bentley, available in red, black, green, or white. Working LED headlights, scissor doors, realistic engine sounds, and a high/low speed switch give it plenty of big-car flair. Parents can steer with the remote, too, in case the young racer needs a little help staying on course.

Sources indicate that it reaches about 3 mph and offers up to an hour of playtime, depending on speed and terrain. It’s recommended for ages three to six and supports up to 66 pounds.

Little adventure seekers will get a kick out of this replica Jeep, with its LED headlights, lockable doors, grid windshield, and off-road tires. It includes a parent remote, spring suspension, and a safe and manageable max speed of just 2.8 mph. It comes in five colors besides light or dark pink: black, blue, green, red, and white.

According to recent reports, while this ride-on Jeep replica claims to be for kids aged three to six, reviewers say that because of the roll bar, it’s actually ideal for younger, smaller kids who can easily slide into the seat. Keep an eye on that weight limit.

Sources indicate that this officially licensed G63 brings plenty of grown-up detail to the pint-size package, from exhaust pipes and body decals to doors that open and lock from the outside. A seatbelt and soft-start feature help keep little drivers secure and ease them into motion, while spring suspension smooths out the bumps.

We also like the removable side window: Take it off as your child gets bigger, and the ride-on can keep cruising for longer.

The GoKart Pro 2 adjusts to fit drivers from four foot two to six foot two, with enough battery range to cover up to 15.5 miles. My kids and I had a blast testing it: They eased in with Eco mode’s 5-mph limit, while I switched to Race mode to explore what it could really do around the neighborhood. Four riding modes—Eco, Sport, Race, and Manual—give beginners room to build confidence and experienced drivers more freedom to play.

It’s a serious investment, but the adjustable fit, long range, and genuinely thrilling ride make a strong case for the price.

Kids can take the wheel themselves or let parents guide the fun with the included remote control.

Available in four eye-catching colors, it’s a stylish choice for young car enthusiasts who want to cruise in Lamborghini-inspired fashion.

In a recent development, for kids with dirt dreams, this little red UTV is ready to turn the backyard into a weekend expedition. Its 12-volt battery and dual motors power forward and reverse, while openable doors, LED headlights, a horn, and built-in music add plenty of trucklike fun.

A safety belt, a gentle-start feature, and shock-absorbing tires help keep rides comfortable. It’s designed for kids ages three and up and supports up to 66 pounds.

Recent findings suggest that ever see a kid’s toy and wish you’d had one when you were that age? That’s the way this mini John Deere has us feeling. It’s got two speeds—2.25 and 4.5 mph—plus reverse. (High speed can be disabled for beginners.) It operates via an accelerator pedal and has farmlike tractor wheels for traction on grass, dirt, gravel, or pavement. It also has a cool stake-side trailer and (get this!) a working FM radio. All that’s supercool, but we love the fact that it recharges in just two hours (claimed).

Featuring sirens, speakers, and flashing police lights, this Fire Chief SUV gives children the most realistic experience of driving a fire truck. It’s designed for kids aged three to six years, with a maximum weight capacity of 67 pounds.

Little land movers will feel right at home in this ride-on dump truck. It’s the ultimate fun machine. With two 35-watt motors, it features two speeds when manually controlled by the child using the foot pedal and three speeds (top speed 3 mph) with the parent remote control. It also has a built-in Bluetooth speaker and a working dump bed.

With automatic lifting and an extra shovel, kids can pitch in with the yardwork by carrying leaf piles and debris.

Industry observers note that let’s be clear: This is not a toy for young kids. Older kids, though, will love these little electric motorcycles. Available in MX and SX packages, with 350-, 500-, or 650-watt motors, they come in blue, yellow, or green. The 350-watt version (ages 13 and up) can hit speeds up to 14 mph for about 30 minutes of ride time; the 650 (16 and up) jacks that to about 17 mph with around 45 minutes of ride time; the 500 (14 and up) falls in the midrange. Pricing is relative. All feature dual suspension and riser handlebars, pneumatic knobby tires, a retractable kickstand, and hand-operated dual disc brakes.

Recent findings suggest that while all are undeniably cute and cool, it’s vital to reiterate that these Razor electric bikes are not toys designed for small children. Helmets are mandatory—and professional rider training is a good idea.

If your kid is ready to take to the not-so-open road, here’s what to look for in a kids’ electric car.

While it can be tempting to get a ride-on that your child will grow into and use for years, there are safety risks involved with choosing one that’s too large or powerful for your kid to control easily. Check the manufacturer’s recommendations for age and weight. Some even offer parental remote controls and seatbelts, while others let you remove features like side panels as your child grows.

Industry observers note that electric ride-ons come in multiple styles to match kids’ varying interests. Classic cars and trucks mimic real-life vehicles, offering features like working headlights and sound effects for a realistic experience. ATVs and UTVs are built for rougher terrain with “all-terrain” tires and higher clearances. For kids who love motorcycles, bike-style ride-ons can often include training wheels for added stability.

Most electric ride-ons are powered by rechargeable batteries, typically ranging from six to 24 volts. Higher voltage generally translates to more power and a longer run time, but it’s key to match the power to the terrain and age level.

It has been revealed that models with 12-volt batteries provide a good balance of speed and battery life for mixed-terrain use, while 24-volt versions can handle tougher trails and inclines. Be mindful that all batteries will gradually lose capacity, so check for compatible replacement options if you strategy to use the ride-on for years to come.

Interactive features can make a major difference in the overall experience. Some ride-ons include Bluetooth speakers or FM radios, letting kids listen to their favorite songs while driving. Others offer realistic details such as functional doors, working headlights and taillights, and engine sound effects.

Many models are designed for children ages three and up, but age recommendations vary. Check the manufacturer’s guidance, along with the car’s weight limit and seat size, to make sure it fits your child.

Sources indicate that they can be fun with adult supervision and age-appropriate use. Look for features such as a seatbelt, a slow-start function, speed settings, and a parent remote. Have kids ride in a safe, open area away from traffic, steep slopes, and obstacles.

Speed varies by model. Some top out around 2 or 3 mph, while more powerful options go faster. Lower speed settings can help younger or first-time drivers get comfortable.

Runtime depends on the model, battery, speed, terrain, and rider’s weight. A manufacturer’s estimate is a useful guide, but driving on grass or hills and using higher speeds can drain the battery sooner.

Some models have rugged tires and suspension for uneven ground, while others are best suited to pavement or smooth surfaces. Check the manufacturer’s recommendations before heading off-road, and avoid wet or steep terrain.

It has been revealed that start with your child’s age, height, and weight, then consider speed, battery life, terrain, and whether you want a parent remote. Features such as working lights, sounds, and Bluetooth can add fun, but fit and ease of use matter most.

📅 26 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (906 w)

Breaking: Hormone Therapy May Boost Weight Loss on Wegovy, But Not as Much on Zepbound

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (906 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Females using menopause hormone therapy (MHT) alongside GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy may experience greater weight loss, according to a study presented at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the Menopause Society.
  • Weight gain is a common concern among middle-aged women.
  • It has been revealed that GLP-1 medications have been shown to be effective for weight loss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Females using menopause hormone therapy (MHT) alongside GLP-1 medications such as Ozempic or Wegovy may experience greater weight loss, according to a study presented at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the Menopause Society.

Weight gain is a common concern among middle-aged women. While much of this is associated with aging, hormonal changes during menopause can also contribute to changes in body fat and its distribution.

It has been revealed that GLP-1 medications have been shown to be effective for weight loss. However, the results may vary by sex and reproductive stage.

For example, studies have found that women and adults under age 55 may experience greater weight loss with these medications.

A previous small observational study in postmenopausal women found that using MHT alongside semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, was associated with greater weight loss.

However, whether hormone therapy influences weight loss outcomes with different GLP-1 medications remains unclear.

Industry observers note that to investigate this question, researchers compared weight loss in middle-aged women receiving either semaglutide or tirzepatide, with or without MHT. The findings have not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

The study included 3,855 women with an average age of 57 and an average body mass index (BMI) of 36 kg/m2.

The semaglutide cohort included 2,379 individuals, while the tirzepatide cohort included 1,476 individuals.

The average follow-up in the semaglutide cohort, both with and without MHT, was 26 months. The average follow-up in the tirzepatide group was 17 months for those using MHT and 16 months for those not using it.

The researchers found that in the semaglutide cohort, those using MHT alongside the GLP-1 medication had significantly greater weight loss at 9 months than those not using MHT.

These differences were sustained at 12 and 15 months and at the final follow-up. Those using MHT were also more likely to reach up to a 30% total body weight loss than those not using it.

Recent findings suggest that in the tirzepatide cohort, those using MHT had a modestly greater weight loss at 3 months and were more likely to achieve more than 5% total body weight loss by the final follow-up. However, no significant difference in weight loss was observed at later time points.

These findings suggest that MHT use may be associated with greater weight loss among middle-aged women taking semaglutide. However, the researchers did not observe a sustained, statistically significant difference in weight loss among those taking tirzepatide.

Betul Hatipoglu, MD, Director of the Diabetes and Obesity Center at the University Hospitals Cleveland Medical Center, who was not involved in the study, told Healthline that the findings are encouraging.

However, she also cautioned that people should be careful not to interpret them as evidence that hormone therapy should be added to GLP-1 treatment specifically to enhance weight loss.

“This is an association, and the study provides an opportunity to discuss how menopause, aging, changes in body composition, and metabolic health can be present,” she said.

It is important to keep in mind that the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved certain hormone therapy medications to treat menopause symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. However, these medications are not FDA-approved for weight loss or obesity management.

The study authors noted that larger studies are needed to confirm their observations and to inform individualized strategies for middle-aged females.

In a recent development, sherry Ross, MD, board certified OB-GYN and Women’s Health Expert at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, who was not involved in the study, noted that weight gain is one of the most common concerns she hears from women during menopause. Beyond affecting self-esteem and quality of life, excess abdominal fat can increase the risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease.

“Finding effective, sustainable ways to manage weight is important for women’s long-term health and healthy aging,” she stated.

In a recent development, “I would like to see prospective, randomized studies examining GLP-1 medications with and without hormone therapy to determine whether hormone therapy directly improves weight loss and helps women maintain it over time. In the meantime, treatment decisions should be individualized and guided by a healthcare professional.”.

Ross advised that the decision should be based on your individual symptoms, health history, and treatment goals.

According to recent reports, “Hormone therapy can significantly improve disruptive menopausal symptoms, including hot flashes, sleep disturbances, and mood changes. By helping women feel better and more energetic, it may also make it easier to exercise and manage their weight,” she said.

Hatipoglu noted that GLP-1-based medications, on the other hand, are effective treatments for obesity and can improve notable aspects of metabolic health. Their use should be based on an individual’s weight-related health risks, medical history, and treatment goals.

Sources indicate that “For a woman who has both bothersome menopausal symptoms and obesity, it may be entirely appropriate to consider both treatments. But I would not recommend starting hormone therapy solely to improve the weight-loss response to a GLP-1 medication based on the evidence at the moment available,” she noted.

“It is also important to remember that successful weight management during and after menopause is about more than the number on the scale. Preserving muscle mass, maintaining bone health, improving metabolic health, and supporting long-term physical function are equally important.”.

You should speak with your healthcare professional about the risks and benefits of all treatment options.

Breaking: The 9 Walking Shoes WH Editors Love the Most

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
