In a recent development, LOW-IMPACT EXERCISES might be forever buzzy, but the running community is going stronger than ever. From 5Ks to marathons, lots of women are lacing up to go for a run and getting all the physical and mental health benefits that come with it. Data suggests running is great for everything from cardiovascular fitness to a healthier mindset, and it may even lower your risk of eight major diseases, making it a solid fitness habit to get into. And then there’s the fact that running makes you feel like you’ve accomplished something amazing (because you have).

As a former competitive runner who still throws down high mileage (50 to 60 miles weekly), I’ve learned the right footwear is crucial for allowing you to continue to pound the pavement, and selecting the right kind of running shoe is key, too. The best running shoes for women provide support and cushioning, with the perfect level of fit to help you forget about your footwear while you run.

Sources indicate that while you can skimp on some fitness gear, a quality pair of running shoes is an vital investment, according to Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois “I am very much in the camp of paying for a really good pair of running shoes,” she notes. “It can help really minimize injury in the future.” (Still, if you’re on a tight budget or just want to save a buck, these are our favorite cheap running shoes.).

But, before taking the plunge on racking up miles, it’s notable to figure out what kind of heel-to-toe drop, toe box, stability, cushioning, and heel stack is best for you. Finding the perfect running shoes involves understanding how specific design elements impact your comfort, performance, and overall experience.

There is no right or wrong, as everyone has different needs (and those needs for running shoes differ from walking shoes), but we'll go over the most key factors to consider when shopping for running shoes.

Hoka does it right when it comes to a durable, high-quality shoe—specifically the Clifton 11, which was released in July 2026 in tandem with the higher-performance-oriented Clifton Pro. The Clifton family has been a crowd pleaser in the running community and amongst WH editors for a long time, and with good reason.

Sources indicate that the Clifton 11 is considered one of the brand’s most versatile running shoes, making it a good fit for everyone from beginners to seasoned pros. WH style editor Shannon Zitz says her feet never felt fatigued while she was testing this shoe, even with plantar fasciitis. “There’s technically a rocker shape built into the sole, but it's subtle enough that I barely noticed it—instead, my stride just felt smooth and natural whether I was walking or running,” she says.

It has been revealed that the Clifton 11 has an eight-millimeter heel-to-toe drop to help alleviate pressure on the plantar fascia, and the brand shaved off almost half an ounce from the weight of the model’s previous version, the Clifton 10, primarily through weight-saving revisions to the shoe’s upper. This was the primary change, with Hoka keeping the midsole that we know and love the same.

It has been revealed that these shoes offer maximum cushioning you’ll feel—the same EVA foam found in the Bondi 9 without the extra bulk. Just be aware that these don’t offer any stability innovations for flat feet, which is especially essential if you’re prone to overpronation. As for fit, the toe box does run narrow, but luckily, wide sizing is available.

Read More: Hoka Clifton 11 vs. Hoka Clifton Pro.

Recent findings suggest that on has built an empire out of its highly cushioned Cloudmonster line. But its most cushioned shoe of all is the Cloudmonster 3 Hyper, an impressively bouncy sneaker that’ll make you feel like a gazelle bounding down the street.

It’s generally accepted that the more cushioning a shoe has, the heavier its weight (because of all that foam packed into the midsole). But the On Cloudmonster 3 Hyper manages to deliver a highly cushioned shoe in a relatively lightweight 7.5 oz package. The result is a next-level energy return that feels like it’s propelling you forward with each step.

This sneaker has a soft, breathable upper to minimize foot sweat, along with a highly padded heel collar that lowers the risk of rubbing. I’ve worn a lot of running shoes, and that heel collar may be the thickest I’ve ever seen. There’s a nice, roomy toe box, too.

While there’s a lot to love about the Cloudmonster 3 Hyper, it’s not perfect. This shoe’s $220 price tag puts it out of reach for many, and the tongue is on the thin side (not a deal-breaker, but some people prefer something more padded). Still, if you have the budget for it and like to feel like you’re running on actual clouds, this is a solid choice.

Read More: Best On Walking Shoes.

Think of a daily trainer as the chameleon of the running shoe world. This sneaker needs to be able to be durable enough for regular use, comfortable, and versatile enough to handle higher mileage along with speedier runs. The Adidas Adizero Evo SL was designed with all of that in mind, serving up a highly adaptable shoe that works for nearly everyone. That’s probably why this shoe keeps landing on the feet of runners all over the place.

Recent findings suggest that the Adizero Evo SL has a soft, bouncy feel underfoot and plenty of energy return thanks to Adidas’ proprietary Lightstrike Pro foam packed into the midsole. It’s also relatively lightweight, clocking in at just under 8 oz. The shoe’s peppy sensation and slight rocker shape support your stride but don’t push you forward in a way that feels unnatural.

In a recent development, this sneaker has an engineered mesh upper to let your feet breathe, even when you’re clocking some serious mileage. This shoe has a slightly tapered toe box, which isn’t for everyone. The outsole is also a little flat and isn’t the grippiest you’ll find, but road runners are unlikely to have an issue. While you’re probably not choosing a running shoe based on looks alone, it doesn’t hurt that the Adizero Evo SL looks sleek.

The best shoe for recovery runs is a total workhorse, delivering enough stability and cushioning to keep you comfortable as you move along at a moderate pace. The Brooks Ghost Max 3 is up for the challenge, with a wide, stable base and supportive feel to take the pressure off your joints.

Recent findings suggest that this isn’t a stability shoe, per se—it won’t work to correct your stride—but it still creates a sense like you’re not going to roll an ankle or have any other gait issues as you pound the pavement. The Ghost Max 3 is a heavier shoe, although I haven’t noticed any fatigue or extra drag in it. But this sneaker holds up well to high-volume running. I wear this regularly and have never noticed any durability issues.

Industry observers note that the Ghost Max 3 features nitrogen-infused DNA Loft v3 foam for support and cushioning. However, it won’t give you a sinking-in feel and there is limited energy return, which could be a pro or con, depending on what you’re after. This sneaker also has a jacquard mesh upper that feels a little softer than many other running shoes out there. The Ghost Max 3 provides plenty of room, from the midfoot to the toe box, making it a good fit for people with wider feet. Just don’t proposal to do any speed work in this shoe—it’s a little too heavy for that.

Read More: Brooks Ghost Max 3 Review.

In a recent development, it's clear that Lululemon’s Wildfeel was designed by people who actually do trail running. It has features you want in a trail running shoe beyond just good grip.

There’s a knitted sock-like upper that molds to your foot to keep out pebbles and other debris, along with a toe bumper to protect your feet over rugged terrain. I took these shoes on several runs over a rocky trail near my house, along with a few beach runs, and was impressed at how well it kept the stuff outside from getting into my shoe.

The Wildfeel has a dual-density midsole, which means that it helps give you a feeling of moving forward when you're going up hills and absorbs impact when you’re going down.

It has been revealed that like many other Lululemon shoes, the toe box runs a little narrow. My heel slipped around a little when I first wore these shoes, although that’s pretty common in a trail shoe, and it got better with time and more wear.

Read More: Best Trail Running Shoes.

There’s a wide range of shoes that consider themselves “stability” sneakers, but the Hoka Arahi 8 does a solid job correcting your stride with each step without being annoying. Many stability shoes are clunky and heavy, but the Arahi 8 manages to be lightweight at just 7.7 oz.

According to recent reports, the Arahi 8 features a lot of changes from the previous version, the Arahi 7. This shoe uses special H-frame technology, featuring foam at the inner and outer foot, to deliver a more balanced support system. It’s roomy and comfortable, too. But this shoe is clearly not for everyone.

The level of stability is high, and that constant gait correction may feel like too much for some people. It also isn’t very responsive, so you’re not getting much back from your shoe with each stride other than security. (To be fair, though, that’s what people are usually after with a stability shoe.) Still, the Arahi 8 is impressively cushioned and very comfortable, whether you’re working your way through a long training session or just going out on a daily run.

Recent findings suggest that long runs require plenty of cushioning to support you along the way. The Nike Vomero Plus, which won the award for Best Cushioned Running Shoe in the 2026 Women’s Health Fitness Awards, is here to help. This shoe delivers a fun, bouncy feel that helps propel you as you rack up the miles.

According to recent reports, the Vomero Plus has a roomy toe box and overall comfortable feel, serving up a shoe that makes long runs a little more seamless. That bounciness comes courtesy of Nike’s ZoomX foam, which is positioned along the length of the shoe. The engineered upper is crafted from yarn for a soft, breathable sensation.

Sources indicate that the Vomero Plus provides a grippy outsole, making it perfect for the pavement. But if you’re looking for a stability shoe, the Vomero Plus isn’t it. Its high heel stack and bounciness is too much for that. But if you want a highly cushioned feel as you log some serious miles, this is an excellent choice.

In a recent development, the right race day shoe has the tough challenge of being supportive, cushiony, and lightweight, helping you to hit a PR without feeling like your footwear is holding you back. The Upcoming Balance FuelCell SuperComp Elite v5 is designed with longer-distance racers (think: half and marathon runners) in mind, but can still be an excellent choice for 5Ks and 10Ks thanks to its lightweight (6 oz) construction and solid energy return.

Let’s get this out of the way now: At $265, this is not a cheap shoe. With that, it’s unlikely to be a good investment for the occasional racer. But if your weekends are booked with road races, it’s worth at least considering.

This shoe delivers a locked-in feel, along with great traction to give you more confidence, even over wet surfaces. The roomy toe box and breathable upper also reinforce the FuelCell SuperComp Elite v5’s comfortable feel. This shoe is stable without sacrificing punchiness, helping you to feel supported as you stride. Just be aware that the midfoot and heel may feel a little too narrow for those with wider feet. But, luckily, this sneaker is available in wide widths, too.

Read More: Best Running Shoes for Plantar Fasciitis.

In a recent development, the lululemon Beyondfeel running shoes truly live up to their name. They’re comfortable at the heels (and everywhere), with a heel stack that provides just the right amount of cushioning. It absorbs impact while still feeling responsive, especially during long runs. Plus, the cushioning around the ankle delivers security in every step.

Recent findings suggest that the heel-to-toe drop is also a game changer—it really makes a difference for runners who heel-strike. Instead of feeling the usual jarring sensation from heel-striking, there are smooth transitions from each step. The bounce in the heel also makes it easier to maintain a steady stride without losing momentum, which is a huge benefit for runners who naturally land on their heels. The shoes guide feet to strike with the midfoot instead of the heel.

Sources indicate that these shoes feel slightly bouncy while you run, and offer decent grip for trails and roads, making for a versatile running shoe. If you’re an overpronator, this isn’t the shoe for you—it doesn’t provide enough medial support (on the inside of the shoe). But it’s got plenty of features to make running a dream for heel strikers.

Read More: Best lululemon Shoes Ranked.

According to recent reports, there’s a range in severity with overpronators, and what works for one won’t work for everyone. But the Asics Gel-Nimbus 28 does a solid job trying to please everyone in the overpronation camp. This shoe delivers a feel that’s not too soft or too firm, giving you the support and stability you need without feeling like you’re in a “special” shoe.

This shoe is lightweight for a stability shoe at 8.5 oz, making it good for most runs that don’t involve speed work. It also delivers a solid, locked-in sensation to make you feel secure with each step. The shoe’s OrthoLite sockliner also supports that cozier feel. The Gel-Nimbus 28 feels slightly springy underfoot, which is rare for a stability shoe. (Still, the overall effect isn’t very responsive compared to non-stability shoes.).

Asics in general tends to run narrow and the Gel-Nimbus 28 is no exception. If your feet tend to teeter between regular and wide sizes, you may want to consider hedging your bets and trying out a larger size.

The best shoe for speed work is very different from what you need for distance training or even race day. The Saucony Endorphin Azura is a lightweight (7.5 oz) shoe with a snappy feel that still manages to make you feel stable and locked in as you zip around.

The Saucony Endorphin Azura uses Pebax foam to create a responsive, bouncy feel, making you feel a little faster than usual. It also has a wide and stable base for added security during training. While it’s designed for speed, you can still comfortably wear this sneaker for longer runs and daily mileage. Just be aware that the shoe’s special SpeedRoll technology may feel slightly awkward at slower speeds.

According to recent reports, the Endorphin Azura’s outsole features XT-900 rubber for a grippy feel underfoot, making you feel comfortable pushing the pace. Saucony shoes are known for a narrower fit, and the Endorphin Azura is no exception. If you have wider feet, it may be best to look elsewhere. (It unfortunately doesn’t come in wide sizes.).

In a recent development, maximum Cushioning: This type of cushion feels amazingly plush and has excellent shock absorption, which is essential for long-distance running. While they’re designed to minimize the impact on the joints, they’re not the best for speed workouts unless the shoe has a lower heel-to-toe drop and some firmness.

Medium: If you want to balance speed with stability, medium cushioning is ideal. Too much cushioning can cause runners with flat feet to overpronate more from the bulkiness and softness. So, this type of cushioning is best if you want a more aligned gait.

This is the difference in height between the heel and front part (known as the forefoot) of the shoe. It can impact how your foot lands on the ground when you run. Low drops (0 to 4 mm) are flatter and encourage a natural running style where you land in the middle or front of your foot. They’re great if you like to feel close to the ground, enjoy trail running, or prefer a minimalist shoe design. Medium drop (5 to 8 mm) is a versatile option that offers mid-height and cushioning—this works well for most running styles. High drop (9 to 12 mm) tends to have more height in the heel to absorb impact (this is great for heel-strikers).

Recent findings suggest that this is the height of the cushion under the heel. It’s measured from the outsole (the bottom of the shoe) to the insole (where your foot rests). Higher stacks offer more softness for long-distance running or for those who need less impact on the joints. Prioritizing this means sacrificing ground feel, and for some, that may feel unbalanced given the additional height.

Recent findings suggest that running shoes can provide a slew of benefits to suit your feet, but podiatrists stress the importance of getting a well-fitting shoe. “The shoe should fit your foot well and not cause any rubbing on the toes,” notes Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California “They should feel comfortable immediately upon putting them on and walking around.”.

Consider these areas of the shoe when checking the fit:.

Industry observers note that toe Box: This is the front part of the shoe where the toes sit. Toes spread naturally when you have extra room in the toe box, and this is especially important during long runs since feet can swell. But if the toe box is too big, it can lead to sliding and instability in the shoes.

Recent findings suggest that length: Since feet often swell from pounding pavement, it’s a good idea to have about a thumb’s width away from the tip of the shoe to your toe. If you’re unsure of your size, the best bet is to visit a running store to get properly fitted.

Arch Support: Those with flat feet and overpronators (when your foot lands on your outside heel and rolls inward) will want to look for shoes with enough firmness and high arch support to help keep feet aligned. Too much cushioning can create an unbalanced feeling, which can further aggravate pain. Those with neutral to high arches will have no issues wearing shoes with neutral support. Most shoes specify which arch type they accommodate, so make sure to read their product descriptions. And, definitely don’t wear shoes with no arch support—your feet need support.

The type of running workouts you proposal to do will dictate elements like cushioning, support, and weight. More cushioning is often better with daily training and distance runs. You may also get away with a slightly heavier (but not too heavy) shoe, which usually means there’s more cushioning and stability. But shoes for speed work and race day tend to have less cushioning and a lighter weight, making it easier to move faster. For a deep-dive into the topic of running shoe selection, check out our story about how to figure out which type of running shoe you need.

A stability shoe can help correct gait complications like overpronation, which is when your foot rolls inward excessively when you run or walk. Not everyone needs a stability shoe, but some level of stability is crucial for reducing injury risk when you’re an overpronator. There are a few ways to tell if you overpronate, per Graves: Your feet appear to be rolling inward when you stand in a relaxed position and the heels of shoes you’ve worn are tilted inward.

Industry observers note that you should switch out your running shoes every 300 to 500 miles. An easy way to maximize your shoe lifespan is to have a few pairs that you rotate between runs. Also, if you visually see them degrading, it's time to snag a newly introduced pair.

Recent findings suggest that running shoes can be washed in cold water in the washing machine with light detergent, or spot-cleaned with a sponge. But, you should never put your shoes in the dryer—they can shrink! Instead, let them air dry in the sun.

According to recent reports, A simple at-home way to determine your arch type is the wet footprint test. You simply dip your foot in the water and step onto paper. If you see your entire foot, you have flat feet. Your foot will look like a comma if you have high arches, while a neutral arch will show slight elevation.

I’ve tested dozens of pairs of running shoes to determine which make the cut for the best running shoes for women. As a personal trainer, fitness writer, and runner with years of experience testing running shoes, I put each pair to the test during two-mile runs where I evaluated key performance factors such as cushioning, stability, comfort, support, traction, and responsiveness. I also considered how well the shoes supported my stride and whether or not they helped me maintain a consistent pace. Additionally, WH fitness editors provided feedback on select shoes they love to wear during training and racing.

  • Industry observers note that “its burnt to heck.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Generative artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented wave of scams, from vocal clone politician phone calls to uncomfortably realistic deepfake images. While most of these are designed and coordinated by groups of bad actors hoping to cast the widest net possible, some are the work of individuals simply attempting to pull one over on specific targets. Many AI con jobs are more convincing than others, but one pizzeria owner in Los Angeles almost immediately suspected a recent patron’s complaint once they saw the supposed “evidence.”.

After receiving their pizza from Masa of Echo Park via DoorDash, a customer named “Dana B” demanded a full refund for what they claimed was an inedible, burnt pie. Accompanying their grammatically questionable message was a picture of what appeared to be a charred Chicago-style pizza.

Industry observers note that “its burnt to heck. burnt. black. cant eat it. dont wanna eat cancer…,” they wrote in their complaint.

However, Masa owner Rhonda Reynolds knew almost instantly that the allegation was categorically false.

Sources indicate that “It was impossible. It was absolutely impossible,” she told local news outlet KTLA 5.

Industry observers note that reynolds uploaded the photo into an app called “Is This AI,” which offered a 96 percent certainty that the picture was faked. She even checked the restaurant’s kitchen security footage to be sure. The footage showed an employee boxing a clearly uncharred pizza destined for Dana B.Masa then laid out the facts in a complaint that countered the first complaint, and the app soon reversed its automatic refund initially dispersed to the scammer. But while justice was served this time, Reynolds remains worried that the experience is only a preview of AI cons to come.

“If this is a new frontier, we’re not gonna make through to the other side if all of our time is spent [on scams],” she remarked.

Industry News: 16 Best Wallpaper Brands to Transform a Room (2026): Editor Picks

📅 10 Aug 2020 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2684 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Architecturaldigest

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Shopping for wallpaper is an excellent way to discover just how indecisive you can be.
  • Wallpaper can also do a lot more than cover four walls.
  • Consider these pinstripes a subtle way to showcase your team loyalty.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shopping for wallpaper is an excellent way to discover just how indecisive you can be. Between painterly florals, graphic stripes, and whimsical prints, narrowing down the options is practically a full-time job. And that's before you get into the textures, finishes, and the peel-and-stick versus traditional wallpaper debate. There's a pattern for just about every room, taste, and level of commitment. Luckily, we've done some of the research for you.

Wallpaper can also do a lot more than cover four walls. A scenic mural can feel more like large-scale art, and built-in bookshelves can get a refresh simply by lining their backs. Even a drawer lined with your favorite print can be a delightful little surprise, not to mention a low-stakes project for a first-time DIYer. Whether you're ready to commit to an entire room or just want to test the waters, these are the wallpaper brands worth adding to your Pinterest board.

Consider these pinstripes a subtle way to showcase your team loyalty. This print suits any number of installation methods, whether you prefer peel-and-stick, pre-pasted rolls, vinyl, or grasscloth. There are even metallic accents you can choose for added glamour.

A geometric print awakens a space in a jiffy, and these Bauhaus circles are prime for a midcentury modern abode. Picture it surrounding a fireplace mantle or in an entryway. Adding the print to a ceiling is an unexpected move that gives the space a wow factor.

It has been revealed that wayfair doesn’t miss a thing—hidden amongst their enormous catalog of affordable furniture and decor is a considerable collection of wallpaper. Every print and pattern under the sun is represented here, from chevron to toile to florals.

This tile-inspired temporary wallpaper can work as a backsplash for a “blah” kitchen, on the walls surrounding your soaking tub, or as panels on cabinets. The tiles have a crisp look and, honestly, look pretty close to the real deal.

When in doubt, toile it out. Toile patterns are an easy way to introduce elevated detail. Their classic, subtle details keep things simple, but dynamic. Plus, they work in many different spaces—a bedroom (child or adult), a bathroom, a backsplash, or a living room decorated with early Baroque pieces.

It has been revealed that serena & Lily offers a small, curated collection of nautical, floral, and patterned designs (many that include natural elements like hydrangeas, palm leaves, and sea shells) for dressing up a nursery or bedroom. The color palettes tend to be soft blues, beiges, and variegated greens that play up to the coastal aesthetic.

For Wedgwood fans, this antique-style print is a serene surprise. (Just keep in mind that it’s not removable before taking on a full project.) Pro tip: The brand recommends using a wallpaper liner if you’re working with uneven wall surfaces to keep the finished project smooth.

Here’s another understated option with subtle texture, available in pastels like pistachio, sand, and sky. The muted tones make a great backdrop to any design style, lending the whole room a sense of calm.

While browsing for furniture, we stumbled upon Anthropologie’s robust collection of elevated wallpaper designs that span sophisticated florals and chinoiserie, damasks, and truly special geometric patterns. Their knack for hand-block prints, Renaissance revival, and arabesque designs makes them a no-brainer for any room that you want to be an absolute showstopper. Don’t sleep on their wall murals, too.).

Green bedrooms are trending, but if you want to up the ante on the soothing factor, look no further than this dreamy chinoiserie mural with cerulean-feathered songbirds and lemons to give your space a bit of joie de vivre.

Industry observers note that showcasing Southern artist Jordan Connelly's signature painterly style, these repeating seashells are a non-cliché way to bring a coastal feel to your space. Plus, the tonal color palette makes this great for a child's bedroom or bathroom.

For subtle stripes and vintage-inspired botanicals, McGee & Co.’s small-but-mighty wallpaper selection is there to fulfill your elevated farmhouse needs. Designed to perfectly suit her existing selection of furniture and decor, McGee’s wallpaper serves as a statement finishing touch, one you soon wouldn’t be able to envision your hallway or powder room without. You’ll even find her take on antique Morris and Co. florals through her pastel-hued collaboration.

According to recent reports, this moody floral is ideal for crafting a cozy corner in a bedroom or den, especially in the navy colorway. Pair with the matching throw pillows for a pattern-drenching moment.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes all it takes is a simple stripe to elevate your space. Thanks to its neutral colorway, you can liven it up or tone it down to your heart's content with a blend of upholstery tones, artwork, and decor. Treat it like paint, just with a bit more oomph.

Sources indicate that chasing Paper is our go-to when we want something elevated that has a dash of whimsy. The brand is known for designer collaborations, too. Most recently, Fariha Nasir translated the South Asian art of block printing into wallpaper with floral garlands and tapestry-like designs. All Chasing Paper patterns come in four options: faux grasscloth, performance vinyl, peel-and-stick, and traditional paper. While we checked out samples in all materials, we can vouch for the durability and crisp pattern of peel-and-stick. They also offer tile decals (that happen to work as contact paper to upgrade worn countertops.).

As far as peel-and-stick wallpapers go, the self-adhesive poly-woven fabric of Chasing Paper is second to none. “I am no stranger to putting up peel-and-stick and the Peonies pattern I used for my home office is on par with luxe wallcoverings for heritage brands,” says contributor Yelena Alpert. “The paper adhered securely to the wood paneling, but it had no trouble coming up if I had to realign a panel. The best part is that I did not get any air bubbles—it’s a DIY miracle.” While Alpert opted for the bold red-and-grey colorway that reminded her of Diana Vreeland’s crimson interiors, a toned-down gold-and-cream is also available.

For fans of cabana stripes, this design from Chasing Paper agrees with minimalists and maximalists alike. It’s tough to choose between seven colorways (though we are partial to daisy yellow), which are all great for different purposes: mud rooms, nurseries, beachy bathrooms, or a design-forward living room.

The contemporary meets midcentury aesthetic of West Elm seamlessly carries through to their wallpaper collection, which includes fetching grasscloth designs and designer collaborations, like their latest with design studio Pierce & Ward. Patterns are geometric and playful but not kitschy, and work perfectly for accent walls. You can also find a few animal print designs and artsy figure drawings that are suitable for powder rooms.

Industry observers note that add this organic, playful peel-and-stick wallpaper to your wish list. Those who aren’t homeowners will love how easy the cleanup is for removable wallpaper when moving day rolls around. And when it comes to wallpaper motifs, simple is sometimes better—the soothing neutrals and distinct geometric pattern will elevate and simultaneously calm any room or nook.

In a recent development, let’s say you want something neutral and textured but grasscloth is not your cup of tea. The Piece & Ward Floral Lattice design is a worthy alternative as it gives the wall a 3D moment but won’t compete with furnishings, especially if you’re into warm wooden pieces. Include ceramic pieces in your home decor to give the entire space a layered look.

It has been revealed that the celebrated 19th century British designer, William Morris, was a traditionalist devoted to his craft in the midst of the Industrial Revolution. He taught himself block printing techniques to create more than 20 nature-inspired patterns that encapsulate the Arts & Crafts Movement. His design brand Morris & Co. was established in 1861 and has shown no signs of slowing down as contemporary designers continue to incorporate the wallpaper patterns in their projects. Each wallpaper design is batch-printed in the United Kingdom, making it a good practice to order all rolls at the same time to ensure the dye lots are the same.

The Strawberry Thief is one of Morris & Co.’s most popular patterns and was inspired by the birds that would pop into Kelmscott Manor, Morris’s home in Oxfordshire, to steal the berries from the kitchen. “The gravure printed paper has this heirloom quality that makes it feel as if it is directly plucked from the archives,” notes contributor Yelena Alpert, who has samples in indigo and crimson colorways. “Each cheeky bird is about the size of my hand, and the foliage has this watercolor quality. It would look amazing above wood paneling, painted or not.”.

According to recent reports, part of the Morris & Co., pattern appeal is that each floral motif is actually on a grid, giving it a certain rhythm. Pimpernel, another favorite, is ornate in the way that the swirls repeat without overwhelming the eye. This design is seen in the Kelmscott House dining room and was chosen by Morris himself. It comes in 16 colorways that span blues, greens, and venture into burgundy.

More than just a place to find scalloped accent chairs and fashion-inspired collaborations (Aimee Song and Carly Cushnie, anyone?), Lulu & Georgia also offers wallpaper. Of course, you can find the likes of Morris & Co. and Scalamandre, but the brand also has their own in-house line. Design stars Sarah Sherman Samuel and Jake Arnold have also lent their talents to this stock with luxe grasscloths and ornate botanicals. Here you’ll find perfect pairings for your velvet bed frame or curved sofa.

Designed by Sarah Sherman Samuel, this intricate print is made more luxe with the addition of a subtle paper weave, adding texture to the linework style drawings.

Polka dots are a playful addition to standard pinstripes, creating a whimsical gateway for those more inclined to traditional styles of design.

In a recent development, beloved for their quirky paint color names like Disco Nap (a pale acid yellow) and Silver Lake Dad (a stormy blue grey), Backdrop Home also makes patterned wallcoverings that perfectly color-match their hues. Once absorbed into Schumacher’s family of brands, Backdrop also introduced archival prints, textured sisal, and peel-and-stick wallpaper options. Backdrop Home offers the kind of whimsical designs that you can’t find elsewhere. Swirling snakes and quilt-like geometric prints that instantly liven up any room, and will have you saying, ‘Oh yeah, that’s Backdrop.’.

It has been revealed that taken from the archives of fabric brand Schumacher, Backdrop Home’s iteration takes notes from John Groth’s original 1957 fabric. The sketched horses and riders pair perfectly with the aptly named Ghost Ranch, a warm terracotta-esque brown.

Sources indicate that available in both sisal and plainweave, this geometric print becomes more subtle the more square footage you stretch it across. While wholly impactful in tight spaces like a closet or powder room, this print transforms in large scale, becoming almost hypnotic with its various plum tones.

With a stock full of ornate prints and patterns inspired by historic European textiles, Transylvanian brand Mind the Gap has something for every design style. Heritage-style plaids for the sophisticated sit alongside Eastern-influenced Ikats and jungle motifs for the maximalist. There are also plenty of coordinating textiles if you prefer to pattern-drench your space.

Inspired by upholstery textiles, this maximalist stripe gives the look of fabric-covered walls without the need for a specialty installation.

Vibrant and eclectic, this floral tapestry-style wallcovering recalls early Germanic florals and the brand founders’ childhoods in Transylvania.

York knows wallpaper. The wallcoverings producer has been around for more than 100 years and still dips into the archive to bring back designs from the early 18th century. The Susquehanna Valley, Pennsylvania, factory is the oldest and largest wallcovering producer in the United States. Even if you’re not into heirloom patterns, their designer series includes collections from Magnolia Home, Rifle Paper Co., Missoni, and LoveShackFancy, among many others.

The Italian knitwear company Missoni is now accessible to the more budget-conscious clientele with its new premium peel-and-stick collection (which also includes the iconic zigzags and florals). The Fireworks pattern is almost like a non-dizzying version of the 1990s Magic Eye motif. “I just ordered all three colorways—natural, mauve, and warm grey—to help me decide which one would look best as an accent wall behind my bed,” Alpert states. “Even though it is peel-and-stick, the texture is that of real wallpaper—smooth and velvety!”.

A tonal geometric print adds just enough visual interest without overwhelming the eye. This print was designed by Joanna Gaines and the Magnolia Home team to combine the beauty of an artist's sketch with the structure of a true geometric pattern.

Sources indicate that boutique wallpaper brand Hygge & West are beloved for their colorful takes on botanicals and geometric patterns. With best sellers like the Alpine Garden and Bloom, the brand seems to have expertly mastered the ability to create visually striking designs that never overwhelm your space, no matter how small. Even in a powder room, the motifs draw the eye in just the right way, complementing your space instead of taking it over. However, if you’re a maximalist, there are definitely patterns for you too.

The Arcade print blends Pac-Man-like shapes and transforms them into a repeat that’s not dissimilar from a quilt block.

One of the brand’s best-sellers, Alpine Garden’s colors pop against the black background that adds a bit of moodiness to typically saccharine florals.

According to recent reports, not every home comes with a century's worth of character, but that doesn't mean it can't look the part. Best known for its period-inspired lighting and hardware, Rejuvenation brings that same appreciation for Old-World charm to its wallpaper collection. Think intricate botanicals, heritage-inspired prints, and textural takes on grasscloth and sisal that make even a upcoming build feel storied.

Sisal doesn't have to stay underfoot. This Hoffmann print recreates the natural, woven texture in a peel-and-stick wallpaper, bringing instant warmth and dimension to the room.

The soft blue-and-cream palette keeps the Fencott print's small-scale leaf motif from feeling too busy.

Are you more drawn to the cozy, muted tones of winter or the vibrant colors of summer? At Claret & Key, you can have your favorite season on your walls year-round. The brand offers its wallpaper patterns in four seasonal color palettes, each giving the same design a different personality. And if none feels quite right, you can dip into the brand's extensive color library to create a combination of your own. Designs are also available in traditional, heavy-grade, and removable options.

According to recent reports, romeo's hand-drawn leaves give you the look of a custom mural without having to hire an actual muralist. The trailing foliage gives the walls a sense of movement, making this an especially fitting choice for a reading nook straight out of an English country house.

Nellie, on the other hand, brings a little sunshine to the nursery or kid’s room with its vintage-inspired lemon print. The Spring palette reads more neutral, with subdued tones that keep the citrus motif from feeling too playful.

In a recent development, hang that framed landscape elsewhere—your walls deserve a full view. Crate & Barrel's scenic wallpaper murals turn blank walls into sprawling gardens and leafy landscapes that look as though an artist painted them right onto the surface. Its exclusive wallpaper collection is designed in-house and made in the USA by York Wallcoverings, with plenty of stripes, florals, and textured designs for those who prefer something more understated. If you're having trouble deciding, up to 10 free wallpaper samples should help narrow the field.

There's a reason Jardin has all the charm of a hand-painted landscape—it originally started as one. Painted in watercolor on canvas paper, the tree-lined scene was digitally scanned to preserve every brushstroke and subtle shift in color. The result is a dreamy, softly layered landscape that gives your walls the look of an original watercolor.

Sources indicate that vivaldi puts a wallpaper spin on the classic verdure tapestry. Printed on natural sisal, it even has the texture to play the part.

James Gray on Paper Tiger, Adam Driver, and Why Great Leading Men Need Danger and Vulnerability

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that ONCE YOU’VE GONE to outer space with Brad Pitt and almost gotten eaten in the Amazon, where else is there to head but home?
  • That resulted, first, in 2022’s Armageddon Time, a largely autobiographical story of a young Gray growing up in Queens with his imperfect parents (Anne Hathaway and Jeremy Strong) and loving grandfather (Anthony Hopkins).
  • It has been revealed that the new film once again features characters explicitly based on his parents, this time with the bespectacled father, Irwin, played by Miles Teller and the expressive mother, Hester, played by Scarlett Johansson.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that ONCE YOU’VE GONE to outer space with Brad Pitt and almost gotten eaten in the Amazon, where else is there to head but home? That’s the question filmmaker James Gray asked himself after wrapping the World War I-era adventure epic The Lost City of Z and the celestial adventure Ad Astra. His answer: “I guess the conscious desire was to go back to what I know.”.

That resulted, first, in 2022’s Armageddon Time, a largely autobiographical story of a young Gray growing up in Queens with his imperfect parents (Anne Hathaway and Jeremy Strong) and loving grandfather (Anthony Hopkins). His latest film, Paper Tiger, was originally conceived as a sequel to that one, but eventually settled into a separate mostly autobiographical and intimate tale of the director’s youth.

It has been revealed that the new film once again features characters explicitly based on his parents, this time with the bespectacled father, Irwin, played by Miles Teller and the expressive mother, Hester, played by Scarlett Johansson. Naive Irwin gets drawn into a sketchy business plan by his brash brother Gary, a former cop and ambitious entrepreneur played by Adam Driver—and things only go south when Irwin proudly decides to show his new venture off to his sons and sees something he should not have.

Paper Tiger also marks a return to Gray’s roots as a teller of crime stories that will stop you in your tracks. (Longtime fans will remember he made his directorial debut with the Tim Roth-led hitman thriller Little Odessa in 1994.) But what could be just another crime drama in the hands of a lesser filmmaker becomes a grounded human story about the downside of ambition with Gray. His films are arresting because they feel like they could happen to you, too.

In a recent development, this new film, then, allowed the 57-year-old director to continue doing what he’s done his whole career: tell stories that, while lightly fictionalized, are still, at their core, true—regardless of genre. “I don’t see the movies as ‘crime dramas,’ even though clearly that’s what they are, because that’s part of the fabric of my young life growing up,” he indicates. “In my father’s case, and in my family’s case, it’s in our DNA. And so, for me, what is simply a memory of some sort, becomes quantifiable as a crime drama. Really, what you’re seeing is me trying to be very sincere with you about my own experience.”.

Sources indicate that it’s a story that’s been deep within him for a long time—and one he’s glad to have finally purged. “Now that I’ve gotten out of my system a little, I’m ready to expand the palette again,” he indicates.

As Paper Tiger expands to a nationwide release in theaters, Gray spoke with Men’s Health about finding great leading men, mining his life for stories, and the key to making everything personal.

Plus—read Gray’s take on his former Lost City of Z star Robert Pattinson as James Bond, from just a couple of days before the casting became official.

According to recent reports, MEN’S HEALTH: You’ve worked with stars like Brad Pitt, Joaquin Phoenix, and Charlie Hunnam, and now Paper Tiger adds Adam Driver and Miles Teller to that list. So, what makes a great leading man?

It has been revealed that JAMES GRAY: To be completely candid, some aspect of what you’re asking is unknowable until you see it on screen. It’s funny, I was reading about the casting of Peter O’Toole in Lawrence of Arabia. He had never done anything on screen, and all of a sudden they put him in the movie, and there’s magic. There are other people who you try to put in movies over and over again, and it never really clicks, for whatever reason. There’s an intangible quality to a great actor that we almost never can put our finger on.

In a recent development, that stated, I’m looking for an ability to convey two things at once: danger and vulnerability. A sensitivity. Often, what you find is it comes from intelligence. I’ve never worked with a great dumb actor. It does not exist. If the actor is marvelous—and I’ve been lucky enough to work with almost exclusively great actors—they are all brilliant in an emotional way. Does it mean they can quote Proust? No, but that doesn’t matter. They have an emotional awareness, and they can read a room, and they have a shrewdness. All of this stuff goes into the work, because if you have a close-up of an actor, you can immediately see what they’re thinking, if they are thinking. I’m looking for both danger and vulnerability, in kind of equal measure. And you see it over and over in great performances. In fact, I can only think of one performance in all of cinema history, really only one, that is both great and has no danger in it, and that would be what Jeff Bridges does in The Significant Lebowski. It has no danger at all, but it’s still a great performance. I’m not exactly sure how he pulled it off—it’s a real achievement. Maybe because he’s so sensitive and lovable in it that you fall for him, you know? But almost always, you have to have that aspect.

MH: When you’re casting for movies like Paper Tiger and Armageddon Time, which are ostensibly based on your own life, do you feel more of a pressure to make sure you get it right, as opposed to a story you’re perhaps a layer removed from, like The Lost City of Z?

Sources indicate that JG: It’s funny, I’m not sure how much difference there is. I know Lost City of Z is about a guy in Edwardian England going into Amazonia, but when I was conceiving of that movie, I never tried to distance myself from Percy Fawcett at all. I tried to, in fact, invest myself in him. He was a dreamer, someone who felt slighted by the system, and he wanted to prove himself over and over again. He didn’t have medals. He wanted to be celebrated, and he finally gets celebrated, and he needs more. All of that is in us.

Industry observers note that so, your question is a very good one, but in all truth, I’m trying—and maybe you don’t succeed, of course—in all cases to put myself into the work. That’s what I would say is making something personal. That’s very different from making something autobiographical. Autobiographical adheres to the facts of your life, and it is true—these last two pictures have been quite autobiographical. But that’s just so that hopefully I have an easier time in getting at what it is that I’m thinking about. They’re different modes, but you’re still trying to do the same thing, which is to get at your interiority.

MH: Miles Teller plays a character based on your father. I’ve never seen him do anything like what he does in Paper Tiger. What sold you on him?

JG: I had seen a bunch of his work, and I’d also spoken to my esteemed assistant director, a wonderful, beautiful man named Doug Torres, who’d worked on a movie with Miles Teller. I knew about him through him, and also the people that had worked with him. I had seen a film called Bleed for This, where he plays Vinny Pazienza, and his performance has what we were just talking about. He’s a boxer, he has a toughness, but it’s a very vulnerable performance. I didn’t want to lean into the nebbish, schlub aspect to the character at all. I wanted the character to have a certain fortitude, because then the vulnerability can really come through. In other words, if you’re just casting a movie and the guy is a nerd or whatever, and you’re watching a nerd be nerdy, it’s not that interesting. What I found was that Miles has an alpha quality, but to see a tenderness inside of that was the thing that really interested me. And I saw it in that film.

MH: Adam Driver is a sensational actor too. What was the appeal and experience of working with Adam?

In a recent development, JG: Adam has a very powerful onscreen dark quality, but he’s also open. He does completely different things from take to take. He’s always trying to find something new, something inventive. And he has tremendous craft. You can tell he’s really studied, and so you have both the craft and also he’s not in a rut. It’s just small things sometimes that you fall in love with. You’ve seen the film—he comes into the house, he brings Peter Luger’s, and he grabs the lamp, you know? A piece of set dressing. And he holds it under his face, and he claims, “Tonight, Luger’s is coming to us.” So, all of a sudden, he’s like a showman. It’s these little touches, where he understands character. And again, I know I’m repeating myself—this comes from intelligence. He’s incredibly intelligent. He sees bullshit a mile away. That is a very good thing for an actor. He is a truth-teller. Great actors are truth machines. They will not let you lie in a scene. They are always open to the moment.

In a recent development, MH: That character is fascinating to me, because in other movies like this, he might turn into a villain. But your story plays with such shades of gray, and it really stands out.

JG: The idea was to set up a scenario where you see the guy and your immediate impression might be “Oh, he’s a cop, he’s bringing food over. He must be a jerk, or he’s trying to scheme, or something.” But in fact it turns out the exact opposite; he had nothing but very pure intentions, and winds up sacrificing himself. That was very much part of taking the audience’s expectations and subverting them. Now, when you do something like that, you’re going to have, hopefully, a small percentage of the audience, whining and complaining, telling you What are you doing there? How could he be naive? But you’re also going to have a large percentage of the audience that’s going to embrace the fact that it’s not a cliché. I was leaning into the sense Adam has as an actor, saying, “Yes, but we’re going to trick you.” And in the end, he’s going to have a generosity and a nobility to his character.

Recent findings suggest that MH: Adam’s character is really brash and confident—it seems like he’s used to getting what he wants and isn’t afraid to kick some ass. Miles’s character, on the other hand, is a lot more reserved and sometimes naive. How did you go about designing the story around these two guys who each carry a very different brand of masculinity and see the world in different ways?

In a recent development, JG: It’s interesting you bring that up, because the operating principle of the movie… I was up very late one night, and I was watching—as one would—C-SPAN, I guess to try to put myself to sleep. And sometimes they televise the speeches that CEOs give at Davos, or that kind of thing. And I saw the CEO of a large corporation, and he was giving a speech, and he said “95% of people don’t know there’s a game.” He said, “Of the remaining 5%, 4% know there’s a game and don’t know how to play it, and then the top 1% know how to play it, and will win.”.

Industry observers note that I think his percentages are off—I think there are a lot more people who know there’s a game but don’t know how to play it, and that’s why we have a lot of anger in the world. But I thought of the story this way. You have Gary, a character who knows there’s a game, and knows how to play it, but he won’t make the ethical and moral compromises to win. You’ve got Irwin, who knows there’s a game, but has no idea how to play it. He’s smart—he’s an engineer. But he’s not shrewd. It’s a very different intelligence. And then you’ve got Scarlett, who probably knows there’s a game and maybe even knows how to play it, but fate has a different plan for her. So, the movie was organized along these principles. That this idea that our society always rewards the smartest and best, that it’s a meritocracy, is not really true. It rewards a certain kind of smarts, along with a certain kind of willingness to compromise. I saw Adam and Miles in this framework.

MH: Do you often find the germ of an idea in mundane places like watching C-SPAN in the middle of the night?

Recent findings suggest that JG: One of the horrible things about creativity, and it’s also one of the truths, is that it is a very mercurial, impatient, sometimes too patient, thing, and sometimes ideas come to you in the most random of ways. The biggest obligation you have to your imagination is your willingness to make the random idea connect. In other words, the essence of creativity is your ability to make connections. So, sometimes, you get inspiration from totally bizarre sources that you’d never imagine. It’s up to your imagination to be open to the randomness of these connections, and to try and pull from them the source of your idea. It can sometimes be totally different, like, you’re in nature, you get an idea, or you hear someone, a homeless man, say something—that’s an idea. It can come from anywhere. And then we have the idea, of course, of myth, to give it some kind of structure. But the random idea is of tremendous value. It can come from C-SPAN, or it can come from a baby crying. It’s all part of the soup.

Sources indicate that MH: With this movie, as you have so often throughout your career, you’re mining from your own life. I’m sure many of these memories are painful, so how do you protect yourself emotionally and mentally to avoid falling into a dark and difficult place?

Recent findings suggest that JG: It’s an excellent question, and the answer is that you kind of can’t. I wish I could give you a glib response—the way that I protect myself is X—but what I owe you, really, is something that is honest, that is sincere. And I don’t owe you the idea that I should make myself look good, and that you should like me. I owe you my own version of the truth. So, if I’m working, it’s not fun all the time. Sometimes, you have to do things that are uncomfortable, that are unflinching, that are honest. And it’s not always pleasant. We recreated a fight between my parents, when my mother hit my father. Scarlett and Miles created it almost exactly as I recall it. This is my job. That’s why I do it. I do it to give it to you. And through that, you find the air of compassion and sympathy for a collective experience.

According to recent reports, in other words, you’re not presenting a fantasy that has no relationship to honest emotion. And, by the way, when I say ‘fantasy,’ I don’t mean Star Wars can’t do it. Star Wars can do that. When he claims, “No, Luke, I am your father,” that is actually connecting to something real, in the guise of a fantasy. When I say ‘fantasy,’ what I really mean is the filmmaker is trying to get you to like him or her or them, and that’s not my job. Sometimes you go to these unpleasant places, and it’s my job to cope.

Industry observers note that MH: You’ve mentioned expanding your palette now that you’ve gotten these stories out of your system—do you have anything specific in mind? Is there anything you haven’t done yet that you want to try to tackle?

It has been revealed that JG: I would love to do a Western. I would love to do a horror movie. I can’t believe I’m going to say this—I would love to do a musical. I don’t know what kind of shape the musical would take, but all of these genres are different forms of expression of the same ideas. I find the Westerns of John Ford unbelievably powerful to this day, because they’re always expressing something that’s inside Ford. Especially the films he made after World War II, which have such a thread of loss in them. And they’re very powerful to this day. You see John Wayne struggling with moral and ethical catastrophes in The Searchers, and you see a kind of post-war reckoning with what was a catastrophe of moral proportions in World War II, and you see it in John Wayne. You see the person of Ford coming out in that way, and using it in that canvas, the American West. That’s beautiful, and a way into the dark side of our personalities. Really, it becomes about me trying to find a story that will accommodate that, and that’s the difficult thing.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Latest Update: Obesity in Your 20s and 30s May Increase Cancer Risk Later in Life

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Younger adults with obesity may be more likely to develop cancer before midlife than those who maintain a moderate weight, according to a study published on October 26 in the Annals of Internal Medicine.
  • The risk for cancer became higher as weight increased.
  • This highlights the potential importance of weight management in the prevention of early onset cancer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Younger adults with obesity may be more likely to develop cancer before midlife than those who maintain a moderate weight, according to a study published on October 26 in the Annals of Internal Medicine.

The risk for cancer became higher as weight increased. The highest rates were seen in those with severe obesity and abdominal obesity.

This highlights the potential importance of weight management in the prevention of early onset cancer.

Rates of both obesity and early onset cancer are rising among younger adults globally.

This study analyzed data from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. The researchers identified 6,313,338 adults ages 20 to 39 who had no history of cancer and who underwent standardized national health screenings.

The researchers followed the participants for an average of 11 years.

Recent findings suggest that body mass index (BMI) was categorized into five groups ranging from underweight to class II obesity using the World Health Organization (WHO) criteria for Asian populations. Waist circumference was also measured as an indicator of abdominal adiposity.

During the analysis, the researchers adjusted for various factors such as:.

Over the follow-up period, there were 151,893 cases of cancer among the participants. The incidence rate increased progressively based on obesity categories, from 1.84% in “normal-weight” individuals to 2.24% in class I obesity and 2.62% in class II obesity.

The strongest associations were seen in the following cancers:.

Obesity was not associated with breast cancer diagnosed before the age of 50.

Ketan Thanki, MD, board certified colorectal surgeon with the MemorialCare Todd Cancer Institute at Long Beach Medical Center in Long Beach, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study, explained to Healthline that obesity itself causes states that promote cancer formation.

According to recent reports, this current study focused on the Korean population. However, the connection between obesity and cancer risk is a global matter.

Sources indicate that previous research has shown that around 10% of all new cancer diagnoses in the United States are associated with obesity. Obesity also accounts for up to 50% of certain cancers, including endometrial and liver cancer.

The study also demonstrated that waist circumference, which indicates abdominal obesity, may be linked to cancer risk that is similar to that of individuals with overweight.

In a recent development, the study researchers used the thresholds set out by the Korean Society for the Study of Obesity. These thresholds put the waist circumference cutoff at over 90 cm (35.4 in) for males and over 85cm (33.46 in) for females.

These are not universal cutoffs. According to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), waist circumference measurements that can increase your risk of negative health concerns are 101.6 cm (40 in) for males and 88.9 cm (35 in) for females.

According to recent reports, previous research has also suggested an association between waist circumference and cancer risk, independent of BMI. One study highlighted a potential 11% increased risk of cancer in people with a waist circumference over the thresholds, even if they were physically active.

The current study found that males had a higher relative association between obesity and cancer, while females revealed higher absolute risk.

The researchers also found that the absolute risk was higher in adults ages 30 to 39.

Those who presently smoke or who have ever smoked were also found to have a higher risk of developing cancer than those who have never smoked.

“Diet, exercise, and now medications can all be used very effectively to reduce one’s weight and, hopefully as a result, cancer risk,” Thanki said.

He also noted that, due to differences between South Korean populations and those in other countries such as the United States, further studies will be needed to determine how this translates across other populations.

“But I think this trend will likely extend across all cultures,” he said.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When a car is stolen, the thief might take it for a joyride, ship it overseas, or deliver it to a chop shop. Stealing a car and holding it for ransom is considerably less common. And stealing a $460,000 race car before then demanding money for its return? That's a whole different level of unusual. But that's exactly the bizarre situation that apparently recently unfolded in London. According to a BBC report, a British Touring Car Championship (BTCC) Audi was stolen, then someone allegedly contacted the racing team's principal over FaceTime, indicated him the stolen car, and attempted to negotiate a ransom for its return.

BTCC team Power Maxed Racing owns the car. On Thursday, the team posted on social media that their racing Audi had been stolen the night before. The car was inside a trailer, and it was parked at the Excel London exhibition center. The lot where it was parked was locked and had on-site security, but apparently that was not enough to keep the brazen thieves at bay.

Recent findings suggest that power Maxed Racing offered a £25,000 (roughly $33,000) cash reward for the return of the purpose-built racer. However, the story soon took another strange turn. According to the BBC, Power Maxed Racing team principal Adam Weaver got a call "with somebody FaceTiming me showing me the car trying to get the ransom." Weaver reportedly told the person that he needed some time to organize the cash and sleep on the prospect of paying a ransom for the safe return of the car.

According to recent reports, weaver received a much more encouraging call later the same day: the police had found the car and trailer. Both were still in London, and only about 10 minutes away from where they were stolen. Power Maxed Racing went back on social media to share the good news, and to thank everyone who helped spread the word and get the car and trailer back.

In a recent development, in the end, the alleged thieves apparently went through the trouble of breaking into a secure compound and stealing a $460,000 race car, only to have it recovered just down the road. It's unclear whether anyone has been arrested, or if there was any damage to the car or trailer. Fortunately, Power Maxed Racing has its Audi back, and that's what matters most.

Industry News: Endangered, colorful garter snakes released into the wild for the first time

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (526 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, most people have never seen a San Francisco garter snake (Thamnophis sirtalis tetrataenia).
  • It has been revealed that however, conservationists recently scored a major win for the snakes.
  • “Seeing these young snakes returning to the wild represents years of research, collaboration, habitat restoration and careful conservation work,” Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District (Midpen) biologist Karine Tokatlian remarked in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, most people have never seen a San Francisco garter snake (Thamnophis sirtalis tetrataenia). Native only to California’s San Mateo and Santa Cruz counties, the brilliantly colored reptile was one of the initial entries in the United States Fish and Wildlife Service’s first endangered species list in 1967. After nearly 60 more years of droughts, invasive species, disease, low genetic diversity, and poaching, researchers estimate only a few thousand San Francisco garter snakes still exist in the wild.

It has been revealed that however, conservationists recently scored a major win for the snakes. For the first time, 62 of young serpents born at the San Francisco Zoo were released at specific sites across San Mateo County earlier this fall. The successful rewilding of dozens of the endangered snakes marks a huge moment for population rehabilitation efforts, and hopefully clears the way for similar releases in the future.

“Seeing these young snakes returning to the wild represents years of research, collaboration, habitat restoration and careful conservation work,” Midpeninsula Regional Open Space District (Midpen) biologist Karine Tokatlian remarked in a statement. “This first release is an vital step toward building healthy, resilient populations that can sustain themselves over the long term.”.

In a recent development, although slender, the brightly colored San Francisco garter snake can grow anywhere from 18 to 55 inches long. Its eyes are larger than most of its fellow garter snakes, allowing it to keep active during daylight hours. With no fangs and only mildly toxic saliva, the snake is essentially harmless to humans, although its bites are fatal for prey like smaller reptiles and rodents.

The process of releasing young animals like these snakes that were reared in captivity is known as head-starting. It is an effective way to protect creatures during the most vulnerable stage of their lives. Head-starting the first batch of San Francisco garter snakes began in 2025, when conservationists collected multiple pregnant females from a healthy preserve in California’s Midpeninsula. Researchers later released the adult snakes back into their habitats after they gave birth, but kept the infants at the San Francisco Zoo. While there, zoologists conducted genetic testing on each snake to select the best possible locations for their eventual release. Conservationists deposited about one-third of them in the same area as their mothers, then placed the other two-thirds at locations particularly in need of greater genetic diversity pools for breeding.

Industry observers note that as biologists continue to monitor the first generation of head-started snakes, another generation is already waiting for its time to shine. More than 130 garter snakes have been born at the San Francisco Zoo this year alone, with an eye to release them sometime in 2027.

In a recent development, “This species is special in many ways, but unfortunately its critical status is not unique,” added Midpen wildlife ecologist Ariel Starr. “The success of this project and the associated research will not only benefit the San Francisco garter snake but will also hopefully inform the recovery of many imperiled reptile species.”.

The Simple Guide to Finding a Weighted Vest You’ll Actually Use

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
