  • It has been revealed that enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts.
  • In a recent development, walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

YOUR LEGS ARE built for movement, whether you’re running, walking, or jumping. So why do most go-to leg exercises have you planting your feet in one spot?

It has been revealed that enter the walking lunge, a truly dynamic lower-body exercise that’s a perfect complement to exercises like heavy squats and Romanian deadlifts. (A bonus: It’s a unilateral exercise that isn’t the dreaded Bulgarian split squat.) The walking lunge is one of the few strength moves that truly gets you moving. And in doing so, it exposes muscle imbalances, trains balance and coordination, and challenges your core and upper body more than you might expect—all while attacking every muscle in your legs.

In a recent development, walking lunges might appear deceptively simple at first, especially if you have done standard reverse lunges before. And in truth, they can be simple. Here, Men’s Health fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. walks you through the steps to take so that you’re not dragging your feet but making gains toward powerful legs.

Recent findings suggest that FORM IS EVERYTHING with this move. You’ll want to stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, squeeze your glutes and shoulder blades while keeping your gaze at a neutral spot straight ahead of you.

Industry observers note that once you’re comfortable with this slow and controlled movement, you can add weights to build extra muscle and strength. You can hold them at your sides, hold them by your shoulders in what’s called a front rack position, or grab one heavy dumbbell and hold it to your chest in a goblet position. “Regardless of how you hold the load, make sure to keep your upper-body tight,” notes Samuel. “Grip the dumbbells like you mean it, squeeze your shoulder blades, and tighten your abs, too.”.

Sources indicate that don’t obsess over keeping your torso too upright, though, claims Samuel. “Especially as you work with heavier loads, don’t be afraid to lean forward slightly,” he says. “That can help you capitalize on your glutes, one of your strongest muscle groups, with each stride.”.

According to recent reports, when you’re starting out, states Samuel, aim to take a step that keeps your front shin perpendicular to the ground when you lower your torso into the lunge. But as you grow more experienced, you can play with the length of your stride to chase different goals. “If you take very small steps forward,” says Samuel, “you’ll attack your quads more. Larger steps can help you build hip mobility and knee health. If you take larger steps, go lighter with the load.”.

“The greatest benefits of the walking lunge come from how it challenges us while in motion,” claims Samuel. “In addition to building strength and muscle, every step forward challenges your front leg (primarily tibailis and quad muscles) to decelerate your body in space, and then quickly work to accelerate into the next step. That’s building coordination and balance, in addition to training almost every lower-body muscle and building serious strength.”.

You’ll work a number of major leg muscles when you do walking lunges, including your calves, hamstrings, quads, and glutes.

SMALL MISTAKES IN your walking lunge technique can turn the lower body exercise into a potential knee-wrecking disaster.

It has been revealed that you want to land on the heel of your foot first to provide a strong base for the rest of your lunge position. When you get started with walking lunges, aim for a vertical shin as you lower down to the ground to stay at a 90-degree angle in your front and back legs.

Industry observers note that you also don’t want to think of taking a step forward, but stepping out a couple inches by slightly turning your glute. Another adjustment to protect your knee is to shift your knee slightly outward instead of toward the midline. (If you still feel any knee pain during lunges, try a reverse lunge instead).

Keep your torso straight and avoid dipping forward, which you may be more inclined to do if you’re carrying heavy weights for this exercise. Your chest should be aligned with the back of your thigh the entire time. As you get up from the lunge, you want to avoid using momentum. That means no shoulder or torso rocking.

THE WALKING LUNGE is a great way to sneak in some movement on leg day if most of your lower-body exercises have both feet anchored to the ground. Load up some weights, and try to aim for 3 sets of 8 to 10 reps per leg, 1 to 2 times a week. You can alternate each leg or finish up all your reps on one leg before switching to the other. Samuel states that will keep more tension and gives you an opportunity to really focus on the muscle.

An advantage of this move is its versatility, allowing you to do it anytime, anywhere. If you’re crunched for time or in a hotel room, try bodyweight walking lunges. Do it for 45 seconds with a 15 second rest for 5 minutes to break a sweat and build muscle.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Finding qualified equipment operators is hard enough for most mining companies, and the extreme weather, punishing conditions, and oxygen-deprived air of the Tibetan mountains combine to make finding operators even tougher for the operators if this high-altitude copper mine – but SANY thinks they have a solution: fully self-driving haul trucks.

In a recent development, chinese equipment brand SANY has deployed fully 60 of its 70-tonne (~80 ton) payload-rated SKT105ED battery electric haul trucks at the Zhibula Copper Mine in Tibet. Operated by Zijin Minig and Tibet Julong Copper, the mine functions at a dizzying 17,700 foot elevation in a region of the Gangdese Mountains known as the Kailas Range, and the conditions there would challenge the health and safety of even the toughest and fittest operators.

Recent findings suggest that “High-altitude illness becomes increasingly relevant above 2,500 meters,” explains Eacon, in one section of a published paper. “Research involving workers in Andes mines operating between 3,800 and 4,500 meters found that 73% of workers assessed experienced periods of nocturnal oxygen saturation below 85% during their high-altitude shifts, indicating moderate-to-severe hypoxemia.”.

That’s bad news for Zijin’s workers – but the good news here, of course, is that the company won’t be needing many heavy haul drivers going forward.

SANY has been working with Perth, Australia-based Eacon Mining Technology to develop an autonomous haulage solution that uses a full suite of both in-vehicle and ground-based sensors, adaptive vehicle controls, and machine learning that can handle the massive bad trucks even here in the Kailas range.

Sources indicate that “Autonomous haulage offers one way to address this challenge,” continues the Econ report. “Rather than requiring a driver for each truck, autonomous systems allow fleets to be managed through centralized supervision, with personnel overseeing operations and intervening when required. This reduces the need for people to spend entire shifts operating equipment at elevation, while changing how workforce resources are allocated across the mine … depending on the system configuration, some operations can manage autonomous fleets from remote Integrated Operations Centers located away from the mine site, (allowing) personnel to supervise haulage activities from lower-altitude locations, further reducing the need for workers to remain in extreme-altitude environments.”.

The working partnership between the two companies combines SANY’s battery-powered truck platform with Eacon’s full technology stack to create dependable, driverless haul trucks with logic and behaviors that are ideally suited to China’s open-pit mining environments.

Eacon technology is currently operating more than 3,100 autonomous trucks cross more than 40 large-scale mines, including Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan Gold-Copper Mine and at the Norton Gold Fields project in Australia.

According to recent reports, while specifications for this specific deployment weren’t disclosed, the SANY SKT105E trucks (the “D” is, presumably, the wide-body variant) the firm has deployed elsewhere are powered by a dual-motor electric drivetrain, pairing two permanent-magnet synchronous motors with a dual three-speed automated manual transmission. The system delivers 570 kW (~765 hp) of continuous power and up to 820 kW (~1,100 hp) at peak output, with each motor producing some 2,430 Nm (~18,00 lb-ft) of peak torque.

Recent findings suggest that those motors get their electrons from an absolute whopper of a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery pack in capacities ranging from 423 to 642 kWh, depending on configuration. The major trucks also offer regenerative braking to recover energy on downhill runs, while their fast-charging system can reportedly charge the battery from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

How I Had to Learn to Stop Saying “Yes” When I Meant “No”

💡 Key Takeaways

  • For years, I was a girl who would say “yes” when I meant “no.” It was only after I decided to stop drinking that I realized how much my “yes-girl” tendency had fueled my drinking cycle over the years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Tyler Woods.

For years, I was a girl who would say “yes” when I meant “no.” It was only after I decided to stop drinking that I realized how much my “yes-girl” tendency had fueled my drinking cycle over the years.

Over the years, both through my own recovery and my work in helping others break their drinking patterns, I have come to see that most people who eventually come to question their relationship with alcohol don’t have a “drinking problem;” instead, they have a “drinking solution.” In my case, my inability and unwillingness to say “no” had created a lot of problems that I ended up turning to alcohol to solve.

I would say yes to a football weekend marathon when I didn’t even know what a quarterback was, and then turn to a 6-pack to make time pass faster. I would say “yes” to hosting the relative whom I couldn't stand, then try to push away my resentment with a bottle of wine. I would say “yes” to helping out at a neighbor’s garage sale after a long week and end up trying to recover from exhaustion with a few cocktails.

Industry observers note that as I started to help others break their old drinking patterns, I realized I was far from the only person who got caught in this pattern. In fact, I came to nickname this particular drinking pattern “the Yes-Effect Drinking Loop.” It’s one of the 10 most common invisible drinking loops that keep an unwanted drinking pattern alive.

According to recent reports, in most unhealthy drinking patterns, drinking is only what we see on the surface. The Invisible Drinking Loop is a term I created to help people understand the hidden forces that keep their drinking patterns alive. An invisible drinking loop is often driven by the need to solve a problem, fueled by the belief that alcohol can help, and maintained by the habit loop in which drinking has become the default routine to cope with or deal with certain situations or emotions.

In the “Yes-Effect Drinking Loop,” drinking has become the solution to deal with the side effects that arise when a person struggles to say no.

As is true with most drinking loops, simply stopping drinking doesn’t break the loop.

With alcohol out of my life, I found myself sitting through events that I had no interest in, battling the desire to reach for a drink to make time pass faster, hanging out with people whose company I didn’t enjoy, missing the quick mental escape alcohol could offer, and dealing with overwhelming cravings by the end of the day after I once again stretched myself too thin in the effort to please others instead of honoring my own limitations.

Sources indicate that it took me a long time to realize that simply stopping drinking doesn’t solve the problems; instead, it exposes them. I needed to learn to find another way to address the problem that I once attempted to solve through drinking, and that meant learning how to say no.

Learning to say no after years of saying yes is not easy. When faced with a choice between disappointing others and disappointing myself, my default response was to choose the latter. Somewhere along the line, I had been conditioned to believe that fulfilling others’ expectations, even those of people whom I wasn't even that close to, was a way to keep myself safe, liked, and in good standing.

Yet, I failed to see the hidden cost of all the efforts to keep others happy; I kept myself unhappy. So much so that alcohol became the only way I knew how to push down my disappointment, exhaustion, and resentment.

Learning to say “no” started with a radical decision to honor my own preferences rather than automatically prioritize others’ expectations. Don’t get me wrong, it doesn’t mean becoming self-centered or never making compromises in life. But it does mean taking an intentional pause before giving in to my compulsive need to keep others happy. And when faced with the choice between disappointing others and disappointing myself, I wanted to make that choice consciously, rather than by default.

In a recent development, of course, giving myself permission to say no was one thing. Actually knowing how to say it was another. After years of automatically saying yes, saying no felt like a skill I had not yet learned.

Industry observers note that that's why Skill Expansion is one of the core pillars of my approach to breaking an old drinking pattern. Truly growing beyond alcohol often requires us to develop fresh skills and tools to navigate the challenges we once relied on alcohol to handle. For the Yes-Effect Drinking Loop, learning to say no is one of those skills.

Fortunately, like most skills, saying no is something we can learn through practice. Personally, I've found that having a few ready-to-use ways to say no makes a world of difference. That's why I've put together 7 of my favorite scripts for saying no with grace.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, “Since we never raise baby animals alone, we had to find a companion for the remaining poult,” the wildlife center wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, it seems straight out of a Disney movie—wild animals from two different species becoming inseparable friends. And yet that’s what happened at the Raven Ridge Wildlife Center in southeastern Pennsylvania, between a turkey and a mourning dove.

Industry observers note that last spring, the wildlife center received two likely orphaned turkey poults (young turkeys). To calm them down, the team put them with a feather-duster as a stand-in mother turkey. Because turkey poults are easily stressed, they are difficult to rehabilitate, according to a Facebook post by the wildlife center. In fact, one of them didn’t make it.

According to recent reports, “Since we never raise baby animals alone, we had to find a companion for the remaining poult,” the wildlife center wrote. “We paired it with a baby mourning dove of similar size, hoping they would comfort each other while eating and exploring as they are both ground eaters.”.

The pairing turned out to be a raging success. They formed an inseparable bond that Raven Ridge Wildlife Center had never seen before. Months later, the team gave the dove a soft release, meaning the bird could leave whenever it wanted. But he clearly had no intention of leaving his friend. The dove continued returning to the turkey’s cage, and the two would sit near each other on either side of the separation.

“After a few days, we put the dove back in with the turkey, and it was clear they were happiest together,” the wildlife center explained. But “we knew keeping them caged for the rest of their lives, or keeping them just because they were cute, was neither an option nor fair to these wild animals.”.

As such, the team contacted a large sanctuary in Pennsylvania to request a joint release. This way, the duo could choose whether to stick together or follow their own paths. After their soft release, the dove flew into the trees and the turkey started foraging, free to stick together or join other members of their species.

“We don’t know if they’ll stay together, but our team made sure they had a safe place until they were ready to be on their own,” the wildlife center concluded.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that your typical 2023 BMW M2 has an electronically limited top speed of 155 miles per hour. However, the optional M Driver's Package raises that limit to 177 mph. According to the Arizona Department of Public Safety (AZDPS) Highway Patrol, one M2 driver was apparently determined to explore the upper limits of his car's performance before trading it in; a state trooper clocked him traveling 170 mph on the highway, and criminal charges followed.

In a recent development, the incident happened on November 9, 2026, on Arizona State Route 202 near Sky Harbor Boulevard in Tempe, Arizona. According to authorities, an AZDPS Highway Patrol State Trooper spotted the BMW traveling at a high rate of speed and passing other vehicles. Using a LIDAR device, the trooper reportedly recorded the vehicle traveling 170 mph in a posted 65-mph zone—an astonishing 105 mph over the limit.

Police were not going to engage in a pursuit at that speed, however, and stated they decided to use the Highway Patrol Traffic Operations Center to track the vehicle's whereabouts. Eventually the BMW exited the highway, and police were then able to stop the car. At this time, the police reportedly noticed that the BMW didn’t have a license plate.

Police say the officer asked the driver how fast he thought he was going, and the man estimated his speed at approximately 110 to 115 mph. That's still far above the posted speed limit, but nowhere near the 170 mph that had him approaching Daytona 500 qualifying territory. The driver later claimed he hadn't realized just how fast he was traveling, according to authorities.

Why was he driving so fast? He reportedly told the trooper he was planning to trade in the BMW and wanted to take it for one last drive. Hopefully his latest car will be slower than the M2, because as police pointed out in their social media post, at 170 mph, the BMW was traveling approximately 250 feet every second. A crash at that speed would be devastating.

The driver was, unsurprisingly, arrested for reckless driving and endangerment, due to his excessive speed and unsafe driving behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Slapping Turn 1’s bright-green curbing, it’s immediately clear that the GR team has done something really good. I’m driving the Toyota GRMN Corolla at Eagles Canyon Raceway in Texas, and the first 30 seconds of recorded voice notes are just me eagerly repeating “Aw, yeah” at various parts of the track.

Recent findings suggest that the GRMN, which stands for “Gazoo Racing tuned by Meister of Nürburgring,” receives an incredible amount of attention for a car Toyota won’t build more than 730 of. The changes are as juicy as workplace gossip. Ten slots are cut into the underside of the carbon-fiber hood to direct air where Toyota indicates it will contribute to more predictable steering at high speeds. Engineers shortened the front suspension’s bump-stop stroke by four millimeters while adding two millimeters at the rear, helping the car settle over curbing. There’s also a taller first gear and a pinch more torque in the midrange. And finally, an optional oil cooler keeps the all-wheel-drive system happy.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota GR Corolla for sale near 73110.

Recent findings suggest that toyota’s obsession over details is admirable. The GRMN’s improvements over the standard GR Corolla are so subtle that they may go unnoticed by most folks and even some car nerds. I started my track time with an automatic GR Corolla, then switched to the GRMN and back. While the car looks only slightly different, the driving experience is wildly fresh.

According to recent reports, the steering is the first major giveaway. Immediately, the GRMN feels much tighter and more direct in turns than the regular GR Corolla. Turn-in is dramatically quicker, and return to center is noticeably stronger. Initially, I thought Toyota had maybe beefed up its steering-rack slider. Nope. It’s largely the same hardware, but with an aggressive electric power-steering calibration. Adding to the different steering feel is a thinner steering-wheel rim, because even if it saved GR engineers less than an ounce, it still counts.

But it’s the suspension that really shines here. Eagles Canyon is rife with elevation changes, including several corners with curbing that would upset the automatic GR and send it bouncing upon landing. But like a honey badger, the GRMN don’t care. There’s no ugly secondary motion; you certainly feel the curb, but the nose stays flat on impact. Toyota developed special monotube dampers with internal rebound springs to help maintain tire contact, while its bump-stop changes convince you corner exit speeds are higher than ever. It’s the most Porsche-like behavior I’ve experienced in any car that competes with a Hyundai Elantra.

Recent findings suggest that it’s worth noting that the regular GR that I drove wore Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires, while the GRMN was on much stickier Pilot Sport Cup 2s. Some of the additional grip and steering response is absolutely down to the rubber, but the way the suspension manages impacts and keeps the body under control is an improvement that can’t be credited to tires alone.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota GR Corolla for sale near 73110.

There is one exception to the GRMN’s good times that not even GRMN chief engineer Naoyuki Sakamoto could explain. During quick countersteering inputs, the electric steering occasionally delivers an unnatural kick through the wheel. It feels as though the power assist has reached its limit, though just for a moment. We experienced it three times over at least 20 laps, but never during our street drive.

The GRMN uses that same ole G16E-GTS 300-hp turbocharged 1.6-liter three-cylinder. Torque increases by just seven pound-feet to 302, with Toyota concentrating the additional grunt between 4000 and 4600 rpm, where the engine spent much of its time at Eagles Canyon clawing out of corners.

It has been revealed that the six-speed manual gets its own collection of changes. The close-ratio EA68F gearbox has a taller first gear and a shorter third gear, changing how the engine works through its powerband. Engineers even revised the shifter-cable mount to make the action more direct. Having driven a manual GR recently, the difference is obvious. It’s not Honda Civic Type R good, but it’s still really good.

Industry observers note that the GRMN also has additional cooling hardware and a driver-actuated intercooler water-spray system. The only other car I’ve ever driven with one of these was the Subaru WRX STI S209, which would make for a rather interesting comparison test if Subaru still built it. A one-gallon water tank sits beneath the GRMN’s cargo floor, supplying enough water to spray the intercooler for approximately 150 seconds. Toyota claims this can lower intake temperatures by roughly 14 to 20 degrees Fahrenheit. Unfortunately, it’s somewhat difficult to see the status of the system, as there’s no indication in the gauge cluster. Instead, the small button has an even tinier amber light that blinks slowly while two nozzles spray water onto the intercooler. It’s no place to have your eyes pointed while setting lap times, and it left us prayin’ it was still sprayin’.

Sources indicate that the most important update may be the optional oil cooler for the all-wheel-drive transfer unit. During Lightning Lap testing in regular GR Corollas at Virginia International Raceway, we’ve experienced overheating that triggers the dreaded “AWD System Overheated” warning. Toyota’s solution circulates gear oil through a separate heat exchanger using an electric pump, roughly doubling the system’s oil capacity in the process.

It has been revealed that however, the cooler isn’t standard equipment, and installing it involves more than bolting on a few hoses. It requires an ECU reflash and activation procedure, as the system’s electrical demands also introduce a fuel-economy penalty. Toyota installed the accessory on our GRMN before we took it onto the circuit. Its own testing suggests the system will prevent the AWD system from ever entering 2WD mode. That’s promising, although even 20 laps at Eagles Canyon (with the front straight closed) aren’t enough to declare the problem solved. We’d love to see how it handles VIR’s 4.1-mile Grand Course.

It has been revealed that eventually, Toyota representatives politely suggested I take a break from lapping the GRMN, motioning toward the line of other journalists in the pits. Ugh, fine. Later, I got another turn behind the wheel for the drive from the track to the hotel. And what a completely different experience that was.

As in the GR Corolla Morizo Edition, Toyota has stripped the rear seats from this four-door hatchback as part of an effort to reduce weight by 66 pounds. The rear windows are fixed. There’s no rear wiper either, which Toyota says saves about two pounds.

Sources indicate that the GRMN is incredibly loud on public roads. With the rear seats removed, there’s little separating the cabin from the racket coming from behind. Those Cup 2 tires scream over mixed asphalt, their noise changing pitch with every newly introduced section of pavement. On the highway, you find yourself yelling at the passenger next to you, and not because they started talking politics.

It has been revealed that the ride is similarly uncompromising. The same suspension that so calmly devours curbing at Eagles Canyon can make ordinary pavement feel jarring. Even the steering, which I couldn’t stop praising on the circuit, takes some getting used to, as it’s so quick on the street, where small inputs produce immediate responses.

I guess that’s why they didn’t name it the Corolla GR Route 380.

In a recent development, the GRMN Corolla starts at $65,655, which is about $24K more than the standard car. That almost GR86-sized price gap is no small upcharge for a Corolla that’s heavy on track ability and light on everyday ability. It’s also interesting that of the 730 GRMN Corollas being built, none will be sold in Germany, home of the actual Nürburgring; it’s a Japan, Australia, and North America offering only.

At one point during the drive event, one of the GRMNs picked up a nail in its tire, and Toyota had to pull it from the drive rotation to give it fresh Michelins. Rather than sit around and pout (as journalists sometimes do), influencers and editors climbed into the regular automatic GR Corolla for a few laps. The lack of complaining during that inconvenience proves my next point.

It has been revealed that the GRMN’s biggest rival is the regular GR Corolla. The latest car’s tiny yet key improvements make it considerably better on track, but is a few tenths per lap worth $24K? Not to mention the street-driving inconveniences? Maybe, for some. For everyone else, there’s a perfectly good GR Corolla with rear seats that doesn’t require earplugs.

  • You've seen enough GRWM videos to know that plenty of people are incorporating lymphatic drainage tools into their morning routines.
  • In a recent development, these tools are marketed to encourage the flow of lymph, which is a clear, watery fluid that supports fluid balance and immune defenses in your body.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

You've seen enough GRWM videos to know that plenty of people are incorporating lymphatic drainage tools into their morning routines. If you also grapple with regular facial puffiness, it's fair to wonder if lymphatic drainage tools could help.

In a recent development, these tools are marketed to encourage the flow of lymph, which is a clear, watery fluid that supports fluid balance and immune defenses in your body. The idea with lymphatic drainage tools—which include gua sha stones, facial rollers, dry brushes, and more—is to mechanically encourage the movement of lymphatic fluid to reduce puffiness and fluid retention.

According to recent reports, dermatologists say there's something to this. "Your lymph system helps move excess waste and fluid throughout the body," explains Joshua Zeichner, MD, director of cosmetic and clinical research at Mount Sinai Hospital. "Lymphatic massages help enhance activity of the system to circulate excess fluid and depuff.".

In a recent development, doctors may recommend lymphatic drainage massage to people with health conditions like lymphedema or to post-surgical patients, says Ife J. Rodney, MD, founding director of Eternal Dermatology + Aesthetics. For everyone else, the data is less clear on whether lymphatic drainage offers much benefit.

"For everyday facial puffiness, gentle massage may offer temporary improvement, though research on gua sha is limited," Dr. Rodney notes. Note the "temporary" part of what she remarked. Despite what you may hear on social media, lymphatic drainage won't permanently alter your cheekbones and jawline, although Dr. Rodney says this may help your skin look fresher and your features look more defined. "Think of it as an optional self-care step, not a requirement for healthy skin," Dr. Rodney says.

Want to opt into this? There is a range of tools to consider—and doctors say you don't need to spend a ton to get results.

A gua sha tool needs to have at least one smooth edge for lymphatic drainage. But Face Gym's Multi-Sculpt High-Performance Contouring Tool has six different edges to focus on different areas of your face. Long and medium smooth edges are made for classic lymphatic drainage, while shorter sides are ideal for areas around your eyes. The tool even includes rounded teeth for fine lines and a targeted tip for acupressure. (Face Gym has an instructional video to help guide you through all of this.).

Face Gym's gua sha tool is made from stainless steel, which is hypoallergenic and easy to clean. The stainless-steel tool is easy to clean, but any product can irritate skin. It also has a nice cooling effect after briefly popping it into the fridge. While this gua sha tool is on the pricier end, its stainless steel construction means it won't shatter like its crystal counterparts if you accidentally drop it.

Both are used for facial massage, but a roller moves across the skin by rolling, while gua sha uses sweeping strokes with a smooth-edged tool. You simply glide the roller across your face with gentle pressure to support lymphatic drainage. This is another stainless steel tool, which means it's a little more hygienic and easy to clean than its more traditional crystal versions. It's also highly likely to survive in the event of a drop.

The stainless steel has a natural cooling feel against the skin, although you can toss it in the fridge for extra chilliness. This tool is heavier than stone or crystal rollers—keep that on the back burner if you're used to those. It also pairs best with an oil or serum to help it glide smoothly over your skin, so strategy to moisturize at the same time.

In a recent development, dry brushing has the combined benefit of supporting lymphatic drainage and exfoliation at once. But some brushes have stiff bristles that can feel intense—and even irritating—against the skin. Esker's dry brush is gentle against the skin, but still feels firm enough to get things moving.

Recent findings suggest that esker's dry brush has a spa-like feel, along with an ergonomic design that's easy to grip. It's relatively petite, too, making it easy to toss in a bag for travel or trips to the gym. The only downside of that is the handle isn't long enough to reach your back. (That's more of an exfoliation matter vs. a lymphatic drainage problem, though.) The rules of lymphatic drainage still apply with a brush like this—if it feels irritating to your skin, stop. But if dry brushing is something you're into and you want to try lymphatic drainage on areas of your body other than your face, this is a solid choice.

According to recent reports, most people do gua sha on their face with a sculpting stone, crystal, or steel device. But not everyone is into the sensation of moving something hard across the sensitive skin in that area. Skin Gym answers the call with a face brush designed specifically for gua sha.

According to recent reports, the brush is densely packed with soft bristles, creating a feel like you're swiping a really good makeup brush over your skin. It has an ergonomic shape, making it easy to glide over the contours of your face. This brush is pretty beginner-friendly, making it a good entry point if you're gua sha-curious. But be aware that you may not be able to get as much pressure on your skin (if that's even your thing) as you would with a stone or other hard tool. The brush also requires regular cleaning to avoid pushing dirt around your face.

According to recent reports, let's get this out of the way upfront: Vibration plates are a controversial tool. Many make bold claims, like that they can support weight loss or mimic the effects of exercise—those are unfounded. But these plates can improve circulation and lymphatic drainage as a result, as Rachelle Reed, PhD, an exercise scientist based in Athens, Georgia, previously told Women's Health.

FWIW, research suggests that you'll get many of the same circulation- (and lymph-)promoting effects from exercise. But if a vibrating plate is more your speed, the LifePro Waver is worth a look. This machine offers 99 speed levels to allow you to fine-tune the intensity. The motor is also quiet, so you don't have to stress about waking up other people in your home. This plate comes with resistance bands and free online workout videos, too. Just be aware that vibration plates aren't safe for everyone—you should take a pass if you're pregnant, prone to blood clots, or struggle with dizziness, for example. Bachelorette star Gabby Windey also recently shared that she broke her back after cranking up her (unnamed) vibrating plate in the name of lymphatic drainage. Though her account is an individual anecdote and doesn’t establish the typical risk, proceed with caution. But if you're looking for a way to get lymphatic drainage moving around your whole body, this is worth considering.

The best type of lymphatic drainage tool for you depends on where you plan to use it on your body. "These types of massages can be performed anywhere, but are extremely common on the face," Dr. Zeichner indicates. "Oftentimes, a smooth, but firm tool like gua sha is used.".

A roller is another option for facial lymphatic drainage, and is usually considered more gentle than gua sha. For lymphatic drainage other than the face, some people reach for dry brushes and vibration plates.

Sources indicate that for gua sha, Dr. Rodney suggests choosing a tool with smooth, rounded edges with no sharp spots, chips, or cracks. "It should be comfortable to hold and easy to clean," she claims—and that applies to all lymphatic drainage tools. For gua sha and rollers, "you don't need an expensive crystal," Dr. Rodney says.

Dry brushes should also have natural fibers, since synthetic can feel harsh against the skin. Overall, "a smooth finish and gentle technique matter more than the price tag," Dr. Rodney notes.

According to recent reports, there's no exact weight for a lymphatic drainage tool that's best for everyone. Instead, it should feel substantial in your hand—but not too heavy or too light. You want to be able to comfortably use your tool, and allow the tool to apply pressure vs. heavy force from you.

It has been revealed that they may temporarily reduce puffiness for some people, but evidence for at-home tools and broader health benefits is limited. "For everyday facial puffiness, gentle massage may offer temporary improvement," Dr. Rodney says. Dr. Zeichner agrees. "Especially if you wake up puffy in the morning after drinking too much alcohol, not having enough sleep, taking in too much salt, or during your menstrual cycle, lymphatic massages can be a useful tool," he says. Just keep in mind that the effects are temporary.

Every type of tool is slightly different. "The goal of a lymphatic massage is to improve the body's drainage system," Dr. Zeichner says. "That is why the massage should be performed in a particular way." If you're massaging your face, the pressure should start near the center of your face, before moving out and down toward your collarbones. This follows the natural lymphatic flow, Dr. Zeichner says.

Industry observers note that "A few minutes is enough to start," Dr. Rodney claims. "Keep the pressure light—bruising is a sign to stop, not a sign it’s working.".

In a recent development, dermatologists recommend taking a pass on lymphatic drainage tools if your skin is irritated, infected, sunburned, or broken. (That includes inflamed acne, eczema, or rosacea flares, per Dr. Rodney.).

It has been revealed that dr. Rodney also suggests checking with your doctor if you take blood thinners, bruise easily, or have blood clots, heart or kidney failure, lymphedema, or a history of cancer treatment or lymph node removal. "After cosmetic procedures or surgery, get clearance from your treating clinician," she says. "Persistent or painful swelling needs an explanation before it needs a massage.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that autonomous lawncare specialists Greenzie passed a major milestone with their self-driving mowers last week, surpassing 255,000 cumulative robomowing miles. For context, that’s far enough to mow every inch of space between the Earth and Moon.

Greenzie declared the self-driving milestone last week, and it’s genuinely impressive, reflecting Greenzie Powered Autonomy mowing more than 9 billion (with a b) square feet of turf across more than 200 commercial customers, 45 US states, and more than 500,000 equivalent man-hours of mowing.

And, while I might have pointed the fact that Greenzie mowers have covered more miles in its press release than Daimler’s entire hydrogen truck fleet, the organization really seems to be leaning into the Moon angle.

“We mowed to the moon, but the real achievement is the commercial experience behind those miles,” notes Charles Brian Quinn, co-founder and CEO of Greenzie and almost definitely the guy who first came up with the lunar lawncare line. “Every mile represents equipment working on real properties with commercial crews. That experience has shaped our technology, strengthened our OEM partnerships and taught us how to help customers successfully integrate autonomy into their daily operations.”.

Industry observers note that greenzie develops autonomous packages for, and maintains OEM relationships with electric brands Mean Green Electric Mowers (whose Vanquish Autonomous commercial mower is shown, above), and Greenworks Commercial, as well as gas-powered brands like Bobcat and Wright Manufacturing. Regardless of what powers the mowers, Greenzie supplies the self-driving technology and integration expertise, while its OEM partners develop and manufacture the equipment that does the actual cutting, clearing, and whatever else their clients need.

Recent findings suggest that “Successful autonomy requires more than capable technology,” said Steve Bush, chief operating officer of Greenzie. “Customers need to understand where autonomy fits into their operations, how to prepare their crews and how to measure success. We have spent years learning those lessons alongside our customers and OEM partners, creating a more consistent path to adoption as the industry grows.”.

The Mean Green Vanquish Autonomous featured gere is a fully electric, stand-on, zero-turn (ZTR) mower built around an all-day-ready 22 kWh li-ion battery pack and featuring a 60″ rear-discharge mulching deck.

Mean Green claims that the combination of massive battery and the electric motors that drive the ZTR mower and spin up its blades are good up to eight hours of continuous mowing on a charge, with an aluminum chassis and deck helping to keep the machine’s overall weight down for easier towing maximum efficiency.

The organization states the mower can operate in either manual or autonomous mode, with Greenzie’s self-driving software supported by six depth-sensing stereo cameras providing 360-degree vision, RTK-corrected GPS, and visual-inertial odometry for onboard site mapping and precise positioning, which Greenzie says allows the mower to detect obstacles up to twenty feet away, recognize designated keep-out zones, and automatically return to its starting point when called back.

A top speed of 11.5 mph and the ability to repeat saved mowing routes, the Vanquish is designed to give commercial landscaping crews another productive worker without adding another person to the payroll … which, with a $60,000 asking price, is money they will probably still need.

Let’s get some pro-labor rage going in the comments, and don’t forget to mention what kind of paycheck you’d need to get to go work in landscaping 2,000+ hours a year while you’re there.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, apple has built a variety of adaptations into iOS to support the iPhone Duo, so icons and menus will shift if the software detects it’s running on the inner or outer display of the foldable, rather than a standard iPhone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It took a while, but Apple has finally introduced its first foldable: the iPhone Duo is now available in Star White or Night Sky finishes, starting at $1,999 and up, depending on how much storage you want inside.

In a recent development, apple has built a variety of adaptations into iOS to support the iPhone Duo, so icons and menus will shift if the software detects it’s running on the inner or outer display of the foldable, rather than a standard iPhone. In addition, iOS developers are updating their own apps to better suit the two upcoming screen sizes introduced by the foldable.

In a recent development, we’re also seeing several apps built or optimized specifically for the iPhone Duo, to take advantage of that foldable screen. Whether you’ve got the phone or not, they’re worth checking out as a showcase of what’s possible with the new form factor.

Toastie ($2.99) is a rather whimsical game for the iPad, iPhone, and iPhone Duo. The aim is to make the best grilled sandwich you can, and on Apple’s foldable phone you snap the handset shut and open it again to control the cooking time for your toasties.

You can pick different ingredients and bread types as you go, and the ability to partially open the iPhone Duo to peek at your culinary creation is a nice touch. It’s not the most sophisticated cooking sim, but you might be surprised by how much fun it is to play.

Bring some old-school to your iPhone Duo with Tiny Computers ($3.99): With the foldable half open and propped up, the flat half turns into a virtual keyboard, and the vertical half highlights a simulated display from a classic computer of your choice—with 10 to pick from.

The available computers include vintage Windows and Mac machines, plus the Commodore 64; while these aren’t full-scale emulators, you can play around with them and discover some “nostalgic secrets” as you go (including some iconic keyboard sounds).

According to recent reports, there are also gaming experiences specifically for the iPhone Duo to enjoy. Marbles Unhinged (freemium, $2.99 to unlock all levels) is a marble-rolling game that uses your phone’s accelerometer and gyroscope to create realistic physical tilting controls.

Recent findings suggest that with the iPhone Duo half open, one half of the main display becomes the marble maze, and the other half becomes a ramp you use to get the marble moving to the right place at the right speed. There are 10 levels available to play for free before you have to pay.

Simply put, Foldissimo (free, $9.99 to unlock all the songs) turns your iPhone Duo into a virtual accordion. You can adjust the airflow affecting the instrument by folding and unfolding the Apple device—faster folds pump in more air and increase the volume.

In a recent development, there is a selection of classic song tutorials included to get you started, and you can compose your own too. You can also switch to other instruments, including panpipes and a theremin, but that’ll cost you extra. A clever idea, neatly implemented.

If you’ve got a hankering for the days when we carried camcorders around as separate gadgets—rather than just using our phones to record video—then Flipcorder ($4.99) is a perfect iPhone Duo app, complete with a retro-looking interface and workflow.

You can only record videos in 20-second bursts, up to 30 minutes a day, reflecting the limitations of camcorders of yesteryear. When you close the foldable, the outer display indicates your subjects what’s being filmed, which is a smart touch. (And don’t forget to back your videos up.).

It has been revealed that if you remember the Walkman era, then you’ll love Deck-Man ($4.99), which gives the iPhone Duo the feel of a classic cassette player. It interfaces with Apple Music and any music files you’ve got stored locally on your device to give audio playback a retro feel.

According to recent reports, your albums show up as cassette tapes, and there are chunky virtual buttons for starting and stopping the audio—with the familiar fast forward, rewind, and eject buttons here too. The app even includes authentic mechanical sounds, recorded from a real cassette player.

It has been revealed that unfold Your City (free; $4.99 to unlock all the cities) utilizes the iPhone Duo’s foldable form factor to turn the handset into a virtual pop-up book that serves as your guide to the world’s most famous cities. You can even switch between day and night modes.

According to recent reports, it’s a fresh twist on the usual travel guide format, and plenty of care and attention has been put into the details here (nice touches include a Tower Bridge that actually opens in London). Be warned, though: the app may have a serious impact on your travel budget.

It has been revealed that first and foremost, you'll need a weight bench strong enough to handle your training regimen—and even if you're not doing heavyweight moves, you'll want it to support a decent amount of load. That's because it's about more than your bodyweight and the weight you're training with; each time you set up on the bench, there's potential for additional impact. In general, aim for a bench that can support at least 500 pounds; that'll set you up for success in nearly all your training and support more advanced exercises that bring even more impact (such as step-ups and plyometric Bulgarians).

The right balance between stiff and cushioned padding is essential to ensure your bench will stay in good condition with use. Highly cushioned benches might feel nice, but they tend to deform over time, creating an uneven surface. This can also compromise your form during workouts, especially when your spine or shoulders are required to stay in alignment. While most padding is stitched to the bench, some is stapled, which tends to lift away from the bench’s frame eventually. Not enough padding isn't good either, as you'll feel like you're lying on a plywood board.

It has been revealed that if you strategy on using your adjustable bench for flat bench variations, be mindful of the distance between the back pad and seat pad (otherwise known as the ‘pad gap’). Anything larger than 2 inches will be noticeable and may feel uncomfortable during certain lifts.

It has been revealed that in general, the three types of weight benches are flat, adjustable incline, and adjustable incline/decline. The first two are pretty self-explanatory and the latter, of course, adds versatility for decline-angle exercises. "If you're unsure which bench to get, opt for a bench with incline-angle options. Sure, this may cost slightly more initially, but it'll set you up with a bench that can grow with you," explains Samuel. "In general, most website workouts and app workouts assume that, if you're training with a bench, it has incline options. So not having incline options can set you up for frustration. It'll also heavily limit your ability to vary your workouts in fun ways. The incline bench is the most future-proofed purchase option.".

Sources indicate that if you're a powerlifter, or you're buying a bench for a particular program, a flat bench might be perfect. Decline-angle benches open up new movements (especially when it comes to core training), but they're generally unnecessary. Think of that as your luxury option.

It has been revealed that like all home gym equipment, weight benches can take up a lot of room. If you’re tight on space or just appreciate being able to move your equipment out of the way, consider a collapsible weight bench or, at the very least, one with wheels. If you’re after an adjustable weight bench, wheels should be a top priority. Because they’re on the heavier side, this will make stowing away and setting up tremendously easier. You don't want setting up your bench every session to be a part of your workout.

According to recent reports, return policies and warranties represent the manufacturer’s confidence in its product. And with most home gym equipment manufacturers, the better the quality, the better the warranty. In the case that something goes wrong with your bench, it’s important to know your investment is protected, so look for benches that come with at least a one-year warranty.

It has been revealed that as the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, my job is to evaluate the latest and greatest training equipment available. I've had extensive experience with weight benches in both the training facilities I've worked out of and the home gyms I've built. I also consulted with Men's Health fitness experts, editors, and writers on the top weight benches they’ve experienced firsthand. The experts included our own Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. and Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM. The team has tested dozens of weight benches over the years, from high-end, commercial-grade models to budget options.

Our extensive testing process involved a comprehensive evaluation of multiple factors—including size, durability, performance, suitability for different fitness levels, and value—to ensure that we recommend only the best. We tested each weight bench through exercise routines that included flat and adjustable bench moves, covering a wide range of motions and use scenarios. To determine stability and structural integrity, we tested benches at both comfortable and near-maximum capacities, allowing us to assess performance under varying loads.

To gather diverse perspectives, we consulted with our MH Advisory Board and Strength in Diversity trainers, who provided valuable feedback on the top weight benches based on their expertise and experiences. The result is the picks for the best weight benches you can buy right now.

You don’t necessarily need a weight bench to get strong and build muscle, but having one gives you access to a host of exercises (regardless of fitness level), especially when it comes to upper-body training.

Most basic exercises that beginners should master, like dumbbell presses and single-arm dumbbell rows and hip thrusts, are much easier to execute with a bench (especially an adjustable one). Meanwhile, more advanced lifters can get incredible mileage out of a bench by unlocking more innovative moves like half-bench single-arm presses and single-arm rows.

Here's a breakdown of the key differences:.

A flat weight bench is designed with a fixed, flat surface, whereas an adjustable weight bench allows you to adjust the angle of the bench to different incline or, in some cases, decline angles.

"The adjustable benches that offer a decline setting are a terrific value for anyone who wants to get creative with their core exercises while training at home," states Samuel.

Recent findings suggest that "Adjustable benches give you so many more options for your exercises," explains David Otey, C.S.C.S and Men's Health Advisory Board member. "Instead of just working at flat or upright, all of the angles in between can give you variety and diversity in your training options." Those angles allow you to bias muscle groups in different, more selective ways. A flat weight bench limits you to exercises that can be performed on a flat surface.

Adjustable benches offer more convenience overall (especially well-built ones), offering access to more movements and angles. Adjustable benches also offer support for extra movements, such as overhead presses and lateral raises, which can allow for greater loading of those movements in the long term. But flat weight benches win for convenience in two areas. They're generally lighter, so you can more easily move them around your gym, and they're easier to stow when not in use, too.

Because flat weight benches generally have fewer mechanisms and lack a hinge of any sort, they'll be easier to maintain. Adjustable benches don't require a ton of maintenance, but it's worthwhile every so often to check on bolts and caps, and make sure your hinge mechanism is working smoothly.

GLP-1s May Help Lower Diabetes, Heart Risks Better Than Standard Prevention

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (968 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 drugs are more effective in helping prevent type 2 diabetes than the commonly prescribed medication metformin, according to a new study.
  • Researchers said GLP-1s such as Ozempic and Mounjaro were more likely to reduce blood sugar to healthy levels in people with prediabetes and obesity.
  • They added that people prescribed GLP-1 medications had a lower risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 drugs are more effective in helping prevent type 2 diabetes than the commonly prescribed medication metformin, according to a new study.

Researchers said GLP-1s such as Ozempic and Mounjaro were more likely to reduce blood sugar to healthy levels in people with prediabetes and obesity.

They added that people prescribed GLP-1 medications had a lower risk of progressing from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.

The researchers noted that GLP-1 customers also had a lower risk of death from any cause as well as fewer heart attacks, strokes, and heart failure events compared with metformin users.

“The great news with prediabetes is that it’s still possible to reverse the progression of the disease,” mentioned Vinicius de Sousa Barzon Serra, MD, a study author and research fellow in cardiovascular medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, Arizona, in a press release. “This research may add to the case for considering GLP-1 medications earlier for certain patients, rather than waiting until they develop type 2 diabetes.”.

Serra noted that metformin still remains an effective treatment for people with prediabetes and type 2 diabetes.

“This is less about replacing one medication with another and more about discussing additional options with specific patients,” he stated.

The researchers presented their findings at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026 in Chicago. The research has not been published yet in a peer-reviewed journal.

David Cutler, MD, a family medicine physician at Providence Saint John’s Health Center in Santa Monica, CA, wasn’t involved in the study, but stated the findings were “quite impressive.”.

“It elevates the comfort of prescribing GLP-1 drugs as a front-line treatment,” he told Healthline.

Robert Eckel, MD, a former president of the American Heart Association who was likewise not involved in the study, agrees the research provides more options for patients and prescribers.

Sources indicate that “GLP-1s provide another option for prevention, perhaps as an add-on therapy. However, costs and access to these medications are important factors,” stated Eckel, an endocrinologist at the University of Colorado School of Medicine, in the press release.

For their study, the researchers analyzed the medical records of 256,000 adults in the United States with prediabetes and obesity. About 76% of the subjects were women, and the average age of the participants was 52.

About half of those studied were taking GLP-1 drugs with the active ingredient semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide, or dulaglutide.

The other half had been prescribed metformin, a medication used to help manage blood sugar levels in adults and some children with type 2 diabetes by decreasing glucose production in the liver, reducing glucose absorption from food, and improving the body’s insulin sensitivity.

The researchers reported that the people in the study who were taking GLP-1 drugs had a 1.5 times higher chance of reversing high blood sugar to healthy levels compared to people who were using metformin.

The researchers also noted that GLP-1 medication consumers had a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a 41% lower risk of death from any cause.

They added that GLP-1 medications were associated with 15% fewer heart attacks, 20% fewer strokes, 25% fewer cases of heart failure, and 8% fewer cases of atrial fibrillation (AFib), a common type of irregular heartbeat.

The researchers cautioned that their study is observational and, therefore, cannot prove a cause-and-effect relationship. They also noted they relied on prescription records, so the frequency and dosage at which patients took their medication was not reflected.

In addition, the GLP-1 drugs were grouped together, so individual differences between medications were not considered.

Recent findings suggest that eckel remarked in the news release that the benefits for people taking GLP-1 drugs were probably mainly due to weight loss. Eckel noted that the research results open up a wide range of possibilities.

“This is an key finding because the GLP-1 receptor agonists are commonly used today and this is a population that in the transition from prediabetes to diabetes are at increasing risk for cardiovascular disease,” Eckel remarked in a taped interview alongside the study findings.

It has been revealed that cutler pointed out that several GLP-1 drugs also target blood sugar levels and insulin production. They could be effective in people with prediabetes who don’t have weight management issues.

Cutler noted that these people, however, might be reluctant to take GLP-1 drugs because they may not be experiencing symptoms of their prediabetes but could develop side effects with the medications.

Recent findings suggest that “They would not be getting any immediate benefits,” Cutler said. He added that metformin, which was first used clinically in 1958, remains an effective alternative. “It’s been proven safe, effective, and it’s very cheap,” Cutler said.

It’s estimated that 40 million people in the United States have diabetes, with more than 90% of those cases being type 2 diabetes, a chronic condition characterized by high blood glucose levels that results from the body’s ineffective response to insulin or insufficient insulin production.

It’s also estimated that 115 million adults in the United States have prediabetes, a condition in which a person has higher-than-normal blood sugar levels but not high enough to be diagnosed as type 2 diabetes.

Recent findings suggest that around 5–10% of people with prediabetes develop diabetes every year. More broadly, up to 70% of people with prediabetes eventually develop diabetes.

Medication is sometimes prescribed for people with type 2 diabetes and prediabetes. Lifestyle changes can help reverse type 2 diabetes and prediabetes, as well as prevent the progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes.

Among those lifestyle modifications are:.

Cutler stated the lifestyle changes needed to prevent type 2 diabetes are pretty clear.

“The most vital thing for people with prediabetes to know is they should lose weight, reduce their carbs, exercise daily and, if that doesn’t work, then consider medication,” he noted.

8 Questions to Know If Your Relationship Is 'Fake Happy'

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that relationships can be messy and complicated, yet they remain the most beautiful connections we can form.
  • Sources indicate that research is now unraveling why your authentic self is better than slapping on a fake smile, especially in your love life.
  • It has been revealed that in a study that investigated individuals’ awareness and acceptance of mental health challenges, researchers explored the influence of toxic positivity—the societal pressure to pretend everything’s fine, even when it’s not—on well-being.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Lybi Ma.

Recent findings suggest that relationships can be messy and complicated, yet they remain the most beautiful connections we can form. But what happens when a partner tells you to put on a happy face and to stay positive no matter what—suggesting that you sweep the mess under the rug? This is what psychologists refer to as “toxic positivity,” and it is more common in relationships than we’d like to admit, and detrimental, too.

Sources indicate that research is now unraveling why your authentic self is better than slapping on a fake smile, especially in your love life. In light of this, psychologists can now measure whether your relationship embraces authenticity.

It has been revealed that in a study that investigated individuals’ awareness and acceptance of mental health challenges, researchers explored the influence of toxic positivity—the societal pressure to pretend everything’s fine, even when it’s not—on well-being. According to the authors, “When we force our brain to be in a false state of wellness, we send a message to our brain that whatever the emotion is, it is in some way bad or dangerous.”.

Sources indicate that when we avoid emotional discomfort, we may unintentionally be making those feelings larger and more overwhelming in the back of our minds. Pushing down real emotions leaves a mark, and those feelings sneak up on you when you least expect. Avoiding emotional discomfort doesn’t make it disappear; it just amplifies it.

It has been revealed that relationships thrive on authenticity. Pretending everything’s perfect when it’s not can be like throwing fuel on the flames. Research consistently highlights that being open about your feelings is key to a healthy and stable love life.

Recent findings suggest that in light of this, research in Personality and Individual Differences aided the development of the Authenticity in Relationships Scale, a tool that measures how true to yourself and others you are in your social connections. The scale includes eight items to which respondents rate their level of agreement:.

Industry observers note that researchers have concluded that real-life couples who toss aside the “fake it till you make it” script report more satisfaction and resilience when the going gets tough. The developers of the scale found authenticity to predict higher levels of agency and communion within relationships, as well as greater subjective well-being at the individual level.

According to recent reports, open conversations, mutual respect, and a team mindset should always be the goal. Inauthenticity or toxic positivity, on the other hand, makes for a relationship filled with eye-rolling at genuine concerns, brushing off real concerns, or pretending everything is sunshine and rainbows when it’s not.

Relationships flourish when we acknowledge and respect emotions authentically.

Breaking: Feds Investigating More Than 1 Million Honda SUVs, Vans, and Trucks Over Engine Start-Stop Concerns

  • The federal probe, revealed on Friday, November 13, includes 1.03 million units of the 2024-2026 Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Honda’s automatic engine start-stop feature is under upcoming federal scrutiny, after the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration received hundreds of complaints that engines failed to restart automatically from a complete stop at a traffic light on certain models, prompting the agency to commence an investigation.

The federal probe, revealed on Friday, November 13, includes 1.03 million units of the 2024-2026 Honda Passport, Odyssey, Pilot, and Ridgeline. The inquiry also includes 2024-2026 Acura MDX units. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation received 701 complaints related to the Auto Start/Stop feature.

“To help improve fuel efficiency, the Auto Start/Stop system will automatically shut off the engine when a vehicle comes to a complete stop. The engine is intended to automatically restart when a driver releases the brake pedal. However, the complaints allege that the engines are failing to restart once they have been shut off by this system,” the investigation announcement reads.

While automatic start-stop systems were created to improve fuel economy, Honda seems to be having a recurring issue with the feature. Federal safety regulators previously opened a probe into Honda’s automatic start-stop system in 2025. That investigation included 2.2 million late-model Honda Pilot, Odyssey, Passport, and Ridgeline models, as well as Acura MDX and TLX units. However, the upcoming investigation includes 2026 model-year units. Inquiry documents allege that the two issue populations have different root causes and respond differently to repairs.

According to recent reports, there have been no injuries related to this concern, according to the feds. EPA boss Lee Zeldin stated the agency was investigating improvements or eliminating the technology last year; whether it sticks around in the long run, however, an engineering analysis of the stop-start system should bring Honda and NHTSA together to identify an effective solution to this recurring problem soon.

#52353. Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

Is Tesla rushing out a half-baked Cybercab just to shave MKBHD’s head?

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1200 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.
  • Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.
  • Surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Elon Musk called YouTuber Marques Brownlee “a chicken” early Saturday, hours after Tesla opened invite-only Cybercab orders at $29,990 and Brownlee argued that his famous head-shaving bet isn’t lost.

Tesla has about seven weeks to get a Cybercab into a customer’s hands for under $30,000 before 2027, but the half-baked version of Cybercab that they opened orders for with delivery in December makes it look like it’s just to win this dumb bet.

Surely Tesla isn’t down enough to deliver a half-baked product just to “prove” a YouTuber wrong? Or is it?

In a recent development, after Tesla’s “We, Robot” event in October 2024, Brownlee (MKBHD) stated there was no way Tesla would deliver a Cybercab to a customer for $30,000 or less before 2027. If it did, he’d shave his head on camera.

Musk has taken it personally ever since. When the first Cybercab came off the Giga Texas line in February, he replied “Gonna happen 😂” to a bald-MKBHD meme, which we covered at the time. In September, after Brownlee doubled down in a newly introduced video, Musk wrote: “I guess he really wants to shave his head 🤷‍♂️”.

On Friday, Tesla started inviting “select customers” to buy a Cybercab for personal use. The order page lists $29,990, a mandatory $299 per month Autonomy Subscription, a $1,000 non-refundable deposit, and an estimated delivery of December 2026, only in Tesla’s Texas Robotaxi cities.

As we reported Friday, the car only operates inside Tesla’s Robotaxi geofences. And Tesla’s Cybercab Autonomy Subscription Agreement says it “will not operate” without the $299 plan, bans owners from putting it on the Robotaxi network or using it for ride-hailing, and lets Tesla shrink the operating area at any time.

Industry observers note that so Tesla designed a robotaxi, then offered it to select private owners who aren’t allowed to use it as a taxi. Over five years, that’s $47,631 before insurance, registration, and charging. And you are limited to small geofenced areas. If you stop paying Tesla’s monthly fee, which it can change at all times, your cybercab becomes a paperweight.

It has been revealed that brownlee laid out his case Friday night. There are no deliveries yet, the car is invite-only rather than publicly available, and it can’t be used as a cab outside of the existing geofences. He called it “a paperweight if I take this thing home,” though he admits that last point isn’t technically part of the bet.

In a recent development, the memes are everywhere, so let’s go back over the bet: Cybercab publicly available for under $30k by the end of 2026My hair is safe for several reasons1: No deliveries yet. But they’re estimating starting in December so that’s neat2: Invite only, not actually publicly… https://t.co/NCD2aFbe2c.

Tesla fans fired back with clips from his September video, where he described a car that “will not ship to regular people like you and me for $30k before the end of 2026.” Whole Mars Catalog, an Elon Musk propagandist whose real name is Omar Qazi, told him to “be a man and honor your word.” Musk reposted it, then replied:.

Musk also reposted a Grok answer claiming the current offer “matches” the conditions of the bet.

But around the same time, Musk replied directly to Brownlee’s post about the order page, and it didn’t help Tesla’s case:.

Sources indicate that “It will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval. But the monthly fee is too high. Should match the cost of Tesla FSD and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”.

That’s Tesla’s CEO confirming, a day after launch, that the car can’t be sold outside the areas where it already operates and that its price is wrong. A price that Musk fully controls.

Sources indicate that yes, it looks like Tesla is rushing this out just to win a bet against a Youtuber. Absolutely insane behavior. We’ve seen this movie before. In June 2025, Tesla did a single “autonomous delivery” of a Model Y to meet a Musk deadline, then never did it again.

Tesla always pitched the Cybercab as a vehicle for its Robotaxi network. Now, seven weeks before the deadline, a personal-use version shows up that’s invite-only, Texas-only, banned from doing the one thing it was designed for, and attached to a subscription Musk himself notes is too expensive. If you set out to build a product whose main job was letting Musk claim he won a Twitter bet, it would look a lot like this.

This Cybercab offering is completely broken. The value proposition is awful. As others have put it, it’s a permanent variable rate lease starting at $300 a month with a ridiculous $30,000 down payment.

Besides, the bet was "under 30k." Starting price is under 30k, but a subscription is required, which takes it over 30k, just to use it for one day. They could have given the car away for free, and just charged a fee to use it. Doesn't change the total cost.

What do you get for this deal? A 2-seater vehicle that only works in small, incomplete, geo-fenced areas and has no steering wheel to do anything else with it. Meanwhile, Tesla insists that the Model Y, like the ones used in its current Robotaxi service alongside the Cybercab, uses the same self-driving technology.

You can buy one for $40,000, and you get a lot more car than the Cybercab; then you can pay $99 a month for FSD instead of $300 a month. Tesla is supposed to let current Tesla owners drive without supervision in the geo-fenced areas, which would basically be the same product as what Tesla is offering right now with the Cybertruck, but you are not a slave to Tesla, which can brick your car at any time or change the terms.

This offer simply makes no sense, and Musk is sort of admitting it by saying the price should be the same as FSD, not $300 a month.
